title: THE HIRELING
memory_verse: The hireling fleeth, because he is an hireling, and careth not for the sheep.
introduction: From the name, hireling, it means someone that it is hired to overlook the flock. What brought him into the work is to satisfy his personal needs (Job 7:2). Unlike the shepherd that owns the sheep, his purpose is to take care of the sheep and he derives pleasure in their wellbeing and satisfaction (Psalm 23). There are many hirelings among the ministers presently. They milk the flock irrespective of the problem that took to flock to their place. In Christianity, hireling is anyone who is not your shepherd (Your father in the Lord, who feeds you with the word of God and knows you as one of his flock).
lesson_aim: The purpose of the hireling is self centred
application: Stay within the place of grace that God has positioned you. Running from one place to another would not bring any difference
raw_text:
TOPIC: THE HIRELING
AIM: The purpose of the hireling is self centred
MEMORY VERSE:  John 10:13; The hireling fleeth, because he is an hireling, and careth not for the sheep.
BIBLE PASSAGE: John 10:12-13
INTRODUCTION
From the name, hireling, it means someone that it is hired to overlook the flock. What brought him into the work is to satisfy his personal needs (Job 7:2). Unlike the shepherd that owns the sheep, his purpose is to take care of the sheep and he derives pleasure in their wellbeing and satisfaction (Psalm 23). There are many hirelings among the ministers presently. They milk the flock irrespective of the problem that took to flock to their place. In Christianity, hireling is anyone who is not your shepherd (Your father in the Lord, who feeds you with the word of God and knows you as one of his flock).
LESSON OUTLINES
CHARACTERISTICS OF A HIRELING:
He is a hireling: A hireling is hired to work on behalf. He does not act like the owner. There is always an âI donât care attitudeâ in the character of a hireling. The owner of the sheep will rise to risk his life for the flock so that evil will not happen to them (1 Sam 17:34-35). How many of the prophets or pastor you run to can rise to pray for you? Are they not milking you?
Relationship: There is a close relationship between the shepherd and the flock. The shepherd knows what they are to eat, how they will eat and what will not disturb their health. A hireling is an emergency overseer, intruder or caretaker, who does not know the reaction of the sheep. He can only feed them base on assumption. That is the guess work many of the prophets/ministers outside your shepherd would do. They are not the sheep-owner.
Hireling would not go extra mile to satisfy the sheep. Genuine ministers preach, pray, counsel, guide, monitor and get involved in all aspect of the church membersâ life. They do this without expecting monetary reward. If members give them, they will collect but it is not a matter of compulsion.
Hirelings run away: when the going is good hireling will stay, but when it seems things are not going well as expected, the hireling will go.
Hireling may devise means to cheat. Personal matter should be discussed with your shepherd and not hireling (especially business and marital matter)  Gen 30:37-43.
The hireling hardly disciplines the sheep because they had no relationship to do that. They would rather pamper and raise the sheepâs ego in order to get what they want to collect from the them
LIFE APPLICATION
Stay within the place of grace that God has positioned you. Running from one place to another would not bring any difference

raw_text:
TOPIC: THE HEART OF MAN
AIM: The heart controls every action of man, therefore we should guard it.
MEMORY VERSE:  Proverbs 4:23; Keep your heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
BIBLE PASSAGE: Matthew 12:33-35
INTRODUCTION
The heart is an important part of human part. It is very important to human existence. When it stops working that is the end of manâs life on earth. Bible said we should guard our heart, the world guard means we should watch over what goes in and goes out of the heart.
LESSON OUTLINES
HOW TO GUARD YOUR HEART:
The heart receives blood and pump in to the blood vessels to circulate the blood and oxygen to the blood system. In this manner we should filter what enters our heart that becomes our faith. There are entrants to the heart;
What we hear
What we see
What we read
These things unconsciously become part of us. We are in world where foul words, nudity and heresies are common. We must guard our heart against all these.
IMPORTANCE OF TRANSFORMATION
The transformation of the heart makes the Christian life easier to live (Ezek 36:26). We become like God. The heart is the central system that controls everything. So to live a Christian life, our heart must be purged of filthiness and unholy beliefs and images should not be allowed into it.
Read true Christian literature instead of erotic, romance and other unedifying article
Pray and read the bible daily
Get record Christian sermons you can listen to at your leisure time
Watch Christian films instead of circular movies
Avoid gatherings where the discussions cannot do you any good
Observe the cartoons your children are watching
Observe the books your children are reading
LIFE APPLICATION
It is important to note that it is not all so called Christian books that can be read. There are books that teach heresies too, it is your responsibility to filter it by testing if it aligns with the doctrine of the bible.

title: THE GRACE OF GOD

introduction: As Christians, we chant the grace after the service. Most people recite it but they do not know the importance or power that what the recite carries. raw_text:

Home is the unit of the society that determine the peace of a church, neighbourhood and the nation at large. Christian Child should be properly trained on how to fear God from home and not be left to the society to train them
LESSON OUTLINES
COMPLETE TRAINING:
Parent should be involved in all aspect of children upbringing. Parent should create time to talk with their children and advise them properly. The parents should be involved in the following training of the children:
Spiritual training
Moral training
Home training â how to attend to chores at home
Social etiquette
Career training
PARENTS SHOULD NOT DISCRIMINATE
Parents should not discriminate between their children by loving one than the other. They should be shown love equally. Also, children should be exposed to all work. Male should learn how to cook and the girl child can wash the car. Past generations differentiate their works and more attention was placed on the training of the female children than the male. We should have complete children that are not deficient in any aspect of training.
LIFE APPLICATION
Godly children bring glory to the family, church, society and the nation. It is our responsibility to raise the heritage of God in the way that will please God who kept them in our care.

ERONGBA:  A gbodo kiyesara ni oju ona irinajo Kristeni ki a ma ba subu tabi padasehin
AKORI:  Jeremiah 3:22; Yipada, enyin omo apehinda, emi o si wo ipehinda nyin san; sa wo, awa to o wa, nitori iwo li Oluwa Olorun wa.
BIBELI KIKA: Ifihan 2:1-7
ORO AKOSO
Ipehinda ni ki eniyan tutu ninu emi tabi ki eniyan fi ife akoko sile. O je fifi Olorun sile tabi ki eniyan subu lati ipele kan ninu emi. O je oun ti o ma sele werewere, ti o sile le pe ki awon eniyan to mo pe eniyan na ti pehinda. Eniyan yio rora ma da ese (Luku 9:62). O je ki eniyan tutu, igbagbo re ko si gbona mo.
PINPIN EKO
KINI AWON OUN TI O MA FA IPEHINDA?
Ifekufet
Aini akoko fun adura
Aini akoko fun yiye oro Olorun wo
Kikuna lati wasu ihinrere
Olufe faaji â II Tim 3:4
Ife aye â II Tim 4:10
Pipa ilana Olorun da lati te ife okan wa lorun
Igberaga
Aima wa ipade dede tabi fifa sehin kuro ni ipade
Agabagebe
AWON ABAMO TI IPEHINDA MA NMU WA
Ko ni si ayo â Orin Dafidi 51:12
Pipadanu ibasepo pelu Olorun
Pipadanu awon anfani ati oreofe ti eniyan ngbadun lodo Olorun, fun bi apere agbara Emi mimo ati ebun Emi mimo.
Nini imolara pe oun sofo, wa ni ihoho tabi aisi isinmi okan.
Pipadanu alafia
Pipadanu orun ati awon ere orun miran - Heb 6:4-6
ONA LATI MA PEHINDA
Ona lati ma pehinda ni ki a ma se ayewo ara nipa bibere awon ibere ti o se pataki bi; Bawo ni mo se bere? Bawo ni mo se rin irinajo yi? Se awon iwa ati ise mi wa ni ibamu pelu ilana Olorun? Awon ibere wonyi yio jeki a le pada si oju ona, yio si so itara wa ji.
LILO EKO NA
Ayewo ni igba de igba ni a nilo bi a se ngbiyanju lati dabi Kristi, ki a si pari ere ije wa daradara.

title: TRUE RICHES
memory_verse: But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the LORD which exercise lovingkindness, judgment and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the LORD
introduction: When we talk about riches, people focus on possession of plenty money. True riches is beyond possession of plenty money, true riches are not ephemeral that can vanish in oneâs life time. They are things money cannot buy. True riches are obtained through the grace of God. Human being have pursued earthly wealth and forgotten the true riches that come from God or they have lost the true riches in their pursuit of earthly wealth.

application: Earthly riches may vanish before you die or you will leave it on earth, only true riches stay forever till eternity.

BIBLE PASSAGE: I Kings 3:1-14
INTRODUCTION
When we talk about riches, people focus on possession of plenty money. True riches is beyond possession of plenty money, true riches are not ephemeral that can vanish in oneâs life time. They are things money cannot buy. True riches are obtained through the grace of God. Human being have pursued earthly wealth and forgotten the true riches that come from God or they have lost the true riches in their pursuit of earthly wealth.
LESSON OUTLINES
WHAT ARE TRUE RICHES?
Divine wisdom â Prov 3:13-14
Cordial relationship with God â Phil 3:8
Divine health
Gift of the spirit
The grace to pray and get immediate answer
Talents and gifts
Divine honour
Good name and contentment â Prov 22:1

Earthly richness does not bring satisfaction and fulfilment irrespective of the amount accumulated. There is feeling of a vacuum to be filled. A man who accumulates earthly wealth is never satisfied. title: IWA MIMO

title: BACKSLIDING
memory_verse: Return ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings. Behold, we come unto thee; for thou art the LORD our God.
introduction: Backsliding is growing cold and leaving the first love. It is turning back from God or falling from a level of spiritual attainment. It is a gradual event and may take long time before people discover that the person has backslidden. The person will gradually reverting to sin (Luke 9:62). It is waxing cold and faith is getting weaker.
lesson_aim: To know that we need to be watchful of our Christian journey in order not to backslide
application: Regular examination is needed as we strive to become Christ and finish our race well
raw_text:
TOPIC: BACKSLIDING
AIM:  To know that we need to be watchful of our Christian journey in order not to backslide
MEMORY VERSE:  Jeremiah 3:22; Return ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings. Behold, we come unto thee; for thou art the LORD our God.
BIBLE PASSAGE: Revelation 2:1-7
INTRODUCTION
Backsliding is growing cold and leaving the first love. It is turning back from God or falling from a level of spiritual attainment. It is a gradual event and may take long time before people discover that the person has backslidden. The person will gradually reverting to sin (Luke 9:62). It is waxing cold and faith is getting weaker.
LESSON OUTLINES
CAUSES OF BACKSLIDING?
Lust
Lack of prayer time
Lack of bible study time
Failure to evangelize
Love of pleasure â II Tim 3:4
Worldliness â II Tim 4:10
Adjusting Godâs ordinance to suit personal intentions
Pride
Irregular/withdrawal from fellowship
Hypocrisy
CONSEQUENCES OF BACKSLIDING
Lack of joy â Psalms 51:12
Loss of intimacy with God
Loss of benefits and grace enjoyed from God, for example power of the Holy Spirit and the gift of the Holy Spirit
Feeling of emptiness, unsatisfied
Lack of peace
Loss of heaven and the other heavenly rewards - Heb 6:4-6
HOW TO AVOID BACKSLIDING
The way to avoid backsliding is to regularly examine ourselves by asking critical questions. How did I start? How are my doing on this journey? Are my behaviours and actions in accordance to Godâs ordinances? This question will help us realign and ignite our zeal.
LIFE APPLICATION
Regular examination is needed as we strive to become Christ and finish our race well

title: IMUPADABOSIPO LATI OKE WA
memory_verse: Emi o si mu odun wonni pada fun nyin wa, eyi ti esu on iru kokoro jewejewe, ati iru kokoro keji, ati iru kokoro jewejewe miran ti fi je, awon ogun nla mi ti mo ran sarin nyin.
introduction: Gbogbo ohun ti a ni â owo, ebun ati awon nkan miran je anfani/oreofe lati odo Olorun. Awon ngbe igbe aye won bi wipe lala won nikan ni o fun ni gbogbo nkan ti won ni. title: HOLINESS
memory_verse: Follow peace with all men and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord.
introduction: Holiness refers to pureness of heart, intentions, actions and attitude. It is to be without blemish. This is the behaviour and standard God required from us in order to enter His kingdom. Holiness is the beauty of Christianity. So many things other religions permit, holiness would not tolerate them. It is being truthful, honest and righteous. It is the characteristic of a person that fears God. There is no coercion or hypocrisy. Today, people pretend to be holy when brethren are with them, but they act entirely different at their place of work or with other friends.
conclusion: Holiness is a criterion to see God, God hates filthiness.
lesson_aim: Holiness is what differentiates Christians from others

title: DIVINE RESTORATION
memory_verse: And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpillar, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you.
introduction: Everything we have- money, gift, talents and others are all privileges from God. People have lived their lives as if their efforts alone gave them all they have gotten. No one can obtain anything if it is not given to him by God (John 3:27). As a result of the way they handled these gifts, talents and wealth given to them (I Cor 4:7), they have lost it and fallen out of grace. One major advantage of this dispensation of grace is mercy. It makes room for another chance
lesson_aim: God is a merciful God, there is still room for second chance.
application: There is room for another chance that requires that you retrace your step back to God, the giver of true blessing

title: FIFI AIDOGBA DAPO
memory_verse: O si se, nigbati Solomoni di arugbo, awon obinrin re yi i li okan pada si olorun miran: okan re ko si se dede pelu Oluwa Olorun re, gege bi okan Dafidi, baba re.
introduction: Igbeyawo Kristeni ye ki o je idapo mimo larin odo meji ti won ti ba Kristi pade ti won si ti gba isodotun. Olorun kilo fun awon omo Israel ki won ma se fe obirin ajoji, eyi ni pe obirin ti ko ba ti je omo Israeli (Det 7:1-4). Igbagbo Kristeni ni o nto ise, ipinnu, iwoso ati oun gbogbo ti a nse, fife alaigbagbo je isopo larin awon meji ti igbagbo won se otooto. Dajudaju, enikan yio fi awon nkankan sile fun enikeji. Fifi awon nkan sile yi ni yio bi ilowowo tabi ipehinda.
lesson_aim: Fife alaigbagbo je fifi aidogba dapo.
application: O san lati ma bere ibasepo na ju ki eniyan ma foriti i tabi ki eniyan ma wa ona lati se atunse, nitori iru atunse be e ki i se se patapata.
raw_text:
AKORI EKO: FIFI AIDOGBA DAPO
ERONGBA: Fife alaigbagbo je fifi aidogba dapo.
AKOSORI : I Awon Oba 11:4;   O si se, nigbati Solomoni di arugbo, awon obinrin re yi i li okan pada si olorun miran: okan re ko si se dede pelu Oluwa Olorun re, gege bi okan Dafidi, baba re.
BIBELI KIKA: II Korinti 6:14-18
ORO AKOSO
Igbeyawo Kristeni ye ki o je idapo mimo larin odo meji ti won ti ba Kristi pade ti won si ti gba isodotun. Olorun kilo fun awon omo Israel ki won ma se fe obirin ajoji, eyi ni pe obirin ti ko ba ti je omo Israeli (Det 7:1-4). Igbagbo Kristeni ni o nto ise, ipinnu, iwoso ati oun gbogbo ti a nse, fife alaigbagbo je isopo larin awon meji ti igbagbo won se otooto. Dajudaju, enikan yio fi awon nkankan sile fun enikeji. Fifi awon nkan sile yi ni yio bi ilowowo tabi ipehinda.
PINPIN EKO
IDI TI O FI YE KI O O FE KRISTENI BI TIRE
Eto Olorun ti o pe fun awon omo re ni ki won ni idile Kristeni ti o pe, eyi ni pe oko ati aya je Kristeni. Mase je ki ifekufe tabi ife tan o je tabi ki o fi nkan ti o nra fun o ati awon nkan miran ti o nse fun o lowolowo fi tan o pe alaigbagbo ni ife Olorun fun o.
Kristeni ti gba isodotun nipa iku ati ajinde Jesu. Emi mimo lo ndari iwa ati ise re. Sugbon alaigbagbo je eni ara, o le wu iwa ti o ba wu. (Romu 8:9).
Aigbo ara eni ye yio sele ninu awon ilakale igbagbo enikan si ikeji, fun bi apere awon igbagbo wa lori metalokan, igbeyawo, idamewa ati opolopo nkan miran.
EWU FIFE ALAIGBAGBO
O lodi si eto Olorun â Esra 10:10-11
Yio mu o se lodi â Nehemiah 13:26
O mu ki o soro lati to awon omo ti yio mo Olorun â Gen 18:19
Eniyan na ti subu, yio si ma foriti oun ti o ba ba pada â Joshua 23:11-13.
Fife alaigbagbo le mu ibanuje ba awon ebi eniyan â Gen 26:34-35
Ironu yin ati ona ti e o fi ma se nkan yio yato nitori otooto ni ipa/ilana emi ti e ba dagba.
LILO EKO NA
O san lati ma bere ibasepo na ju ki eniyan ma foriti i tabi ki eniyan ma wa ona lati se atunse, nitori iru atunse be e ki i se se patapata.

title: IBUKUN TI O WA NINU IGBEYAWO
memory_verse: Ki oko ki o ma se ohun ti o ye si aya: be gege si li aya pelu si oko.
introduction: Igbeyawo je ibasepo larin odo okunrin kan ati odo-binrin kan lati di oko ati iyawo. Ibasepo be ye ki o mu eso rere jade ati alafia fun awon mejeeji, idile ti won ti jade, ijo Olorun ati adugbo lapapo. O seni lanu, opolopo awon igbeyawo ni o ki nmu eso rere jade, won si ti gba alafia awon obi awon opolopo oko ati iyawo. O di ipele pe awon odo ti ngbero boya awon o ni ni iyawo tabi oko nitori awon nkan ti won ti ka tabi ri lara opolopo ibasepo.
topic: IBUKUN TI O WA NINU IGBEYAWO
lesson_aim: A da igbeyawo sile lati se anfani fun awa eniyan

BIBELI KIKA: Oniwasu 4:8-12

Fun ajumokegbe: Eleyi ni lati ni eniyan lati ba jiroro, ki won si jo ni Alafia papo.
Fun omo bibi: Igbeyawo je igbekale lati mu eto Olorun nipa ibisi se. Eto Olorun nipe omo yio ma waye lati ara okunrin ati obirin laisi agbere ati pansaga.
O je ona lati sa fun agbere. Ara idi ti igbeyawo fi waye ni ki a te ara wa lorun nipa ibalopo. Okunrin kan ati obirin kan. (1 Kor 7:2-5)
AWON IDI TI ENIYAN KO GBODO FI SE IGBEYAWO
Pe ojo ori oun ti lo tabi oun ti dâagba
Nitori o fe te ifekufe ibalopo lorun
Nitori awon obi nda eniyan lamu

Nitori wipe oun ri eniyan gbe bukata oun
Nitori ewa oju/ara

Igbeyawo njeki a le feran awon elomiran. Ipile igbeyawo ni fiferan elomiran ti ki se idile wa, ife yi ndagba o si njeki a nle feran awon miran pelu.
Igbeyawo njeki a le se aseyori pupo ju bi a ti le da nikan se aseyori lo, ti o ba je awa nikan.
Igbeyawo njeki a le sise lori awon ailera tabi aipe wa.
Igbeyawo je ki a je oluranlowo fun ara wa (tabi enikan le ran enikeji lowo nibi ti won ba jo se ailera tabi ku die kaato si)
Igbeyawo je ki a ni enikan ti a le gbarale.

Igbeyawo ni ibukun, o si dun ti a bar in bi o ti to. Jeki Olorun ki o dari re lati yan.

title: UNEQUAL YOKE
memory_verse: For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father.
introduction: Christian wedding should a holy solemnization between two young adults who have encountered Christ and have been regenerated. God warned the Children of Israel not to marry strange women, that is outside their nation (Deut 7:1-4). Christian faith/believe is what guides our actions, decisions, dressing and all other things, marrying an unbeliever is the coming together of two people with different background. Definitely, there must be a compromise. Compromise will lead to lukewarmness or total backsliding.
lesson_aim: Marrying an unbeliever is being unequally yoke.
application: It is better not to go into such relationship than to be enduring it or looking for ways to correct the mistake, because the mistake cannot be perfectly corrected.
raw_text:
TOPIC: UNEQUAL YOKE
AIM: Marrying an unbeliever is being unequally yoke.
MEMORY VERSE: I Kings 11:4; For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father.
BIBLE PASSAGE: II Corinthians 6:14-18
INTRODUCTION
Christian wedding should a holy solemnization between two young adults who have encountered Christ and have been regenerated. God warned the Children of Israel not to marry strange women, that is outside their nation (Deut 7:1-4). Christian faith/believe is what guides our actions, decisions, dressing and all other things, marrying an unbeliever is the coming together of two people with different background. Definitely, there must be a compromise. Compromise will lead to lukewarmness or total backsliding.
LESSON OUTLINES
REASONS YOU SHOULD MARRY A FELLOW CHRISTIAN
The expectation and perfect plan of God is a complete Christian home for His children, that both parties are Christians. Do not be deceived by lust/love or be enticed with what he/she is giving or doing presently in order to believe that an unbeliever is the will of God for you.
A Christian has been transformed and regenerated through death and resurrection of Christ. His behaviour is being controlled by the Holy Spirit. Unlike the unbeliever, he/she is a natural person and can behave anyhow (Romans 8:9).
There would be misunderstanding in religious believes, like believe on trinity, marriage, tithing and lots more.
DANGERS OF MARRYING UNBELIEVER
It is against Godâs perfect plan â Ezra 10:10-11
It will lead you astray â Nehemiah 13:26
It makes raising godly children difficult â Gen 18:19
You will forever be defeated and enduring the situation â Joshua 23:11-13.
Marrying an unbeliever may cause pain for the extended families â Gen 26:34-35
Your thinking and ways of handling things would be different because you are raised with different spiritual principles.
LESSON APPLICATION
It is better not to go into such relationship than to be enduring it or looking for ways to correct the mistake, because the mistake cannot be perfectly corrected.

raw_text:

Age factor
Sexual appetite
Parental pressure

Financial security
Physical beauty
Believe that marriage will fix the problem
Prophet/Pastorâs instruction

Joy of the wedding celebration

title: JIJE OLOOTO NI IGBEYAWO
memory_verse: Ma fi ayo ba aya re gbe ti iwo fe ni gbogbo ojo aiye asan re, ti o fi fun o labe orun ni gbogbo ojo asan re: nitori eyini ni ipin tire li aiye yi, ati ninu lala ti iwo se labe orun.
introduction: Okan lara awon wahala ti igbeyawo ma ni ni aije olooto awon oko ati iyawo, eyi ni pe okan tabi awon mejeeji tun ni ibasepo pelu elomiran. O je yiye adehun igbeyawo. Eleyi si ti mu ki opolopo idile ma ni ayo ati ibukun ti o ye ki won ri ninu igbeyawo won. Awon kan, papa julo okunrin ri gegebi oun isogo lati ni ibasepo pelu elomiran. Awon miran, papa julo obinrin si ri gegebi ona lati fi ri owo fi kun wonba eyi ti won ni. O je iwa aimo ti ko mu inu Olorun dun (Gal 5:19).
lesson_aim: Jije olooto se pataki fun abo ati itoju igbeyawo re
application: Pa adehun igbeyawo re mo, je ki ile re fi ogo fun Olorun, ki awon eniyan si le fi ile se apejuwe rere
raw_text:
AKORI EKO: JIJE OLOOTO NI IGBEYAWO
ERONGBA: Jije olooto se pataki fun abo ati itoju igbeyawo re
AKOSORI: Oniwasu 9:9; Ma fi ayo ba aya re gbe ti iwo fe ni gbogbo ojo aiye asan re, ti o fi fun o labe orun ni gbogbo ojo asan re: nitori eyini ni ipin tire li aiye yi, ati ninu lala ti iwo se labe orun.
BIBELI KIKA: Malaki 2:13-16
ORO AKOSO
Okan lara awon wahala ti igbeyawo ma ni ni aije olooto awon oko ati iyawo, eyi ni pe okan tabi awon mejeeji tun ni ibasepo pelu elomiran. O je yiye adehun igbeyawo. Eleyi si ti mu ki opolopo idile ma ni ayo ati ibukun ti o ye ki won ri ninu igbeyawo won. Awon kan, papa julo okunrin ri gegebi oun isogo lati ni ibasepo pelu elomiran. Awon miran, papa julo obinrin si ri gegebi ona lati fi ri owo fi kun wonba eyi ti won ni. O je iwa aimo ti ko mu inu Olorun dun (Gal 5:19).
PINPIN EKO
EWU AIJE OLOOTO NINU IGBEYAWO
O ma ndena idahun adura, Olorun o ki ndahun adura elese (Johanu 9:31).
O jeki o soro lati le fi inu tan ara eni mo.
O ma nfa ipalara nipa temi (Gen 3:8-10, I Kor 6:18-20)
O ma njeki oko ati aya ki won ma nife ara won mo, ko si ni si aye ibara-eni-soro mo.
O ma nfa edun okan si eniti a se aisooto si ati awon lokan.
O ma njeki eniyan ma niyi mo (Owo 5:9)
O sese ki eniyan ko arun kogbo gun.
Eniyan miran ni yio jere ise owo eni na. (Owe 5:10)
O ma nyori si abamo (Owe 5:11-12)
O si ma nyori si orun apadi (I Kor 6:9-10)
MA SORA
Lopolopo igba, awon nkan ti o ma fa aije olooto ninu igbeyawo ni aso ti o rewa ti obinrin tabi okunrin miran ti ki se iyawo tabi oko wa wo, ajose igba-de-gba larin okunrin ati obirin miran, aikiyesara ati afe aye. Gegebi Kristeni, a gbodo sora;
Ma fi aye gba isun-mora-eni pupoju pelu okunrin tabi obinrin miran.
Ki awon ololufe ma mura daradara lati fi wu ara won.
Sa fun gbogbo ohun ti o ba fara jo ibi â I Tess 5:22
Sa fun gbogbo ibujoko ati ti ko fi ogo fun Olorun (awon efe/awada ti ko ye)
Jeki ala wa larin iwo ati awon eda abara keji.
Je aladura, ki o ba subu sinu idanwo.
LILO EKO NA
Pa adehun igbeyawo re mo, je ki ile re fi ogo fun Olorun, ki awon eniyan si le fi ile se apejuwe rere

title: FAITHFULNESS IN MARRIAGE
memory_verse: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.
introduction: One of the major issues in marriage is unfaithfulness by the partners, that is a partner or both partners are having extra-marital affairs. It is breaking the marital vows. This has deprived many homes the joy and blessings they should derive from marriage. Some partners, especially men see it as a thing of pride to keep marital affairs while some, especially women see it as a way to make extra money to augment what they have. It is an unholy act and irritating to God (Gal 5:19).
lesson_aim: Faithfulness to your partner is important in keeping your marriage
application: Maintain your marital promises to your partner, let your home give glory to God and be referred to positively.
raw_text:
TOPIC: FAITHFULNESS IN MARRIAGE
AIM: Faithfulness to your partner is important in keeping your marriage
MEMORY VERSE: Ecclesiastes 9:9; Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.
BIBLE PASSAGE: Malachi 2:13-16
INTRODUCTION
One of the major issues in marriage is unfaithfulness by the partners, that is a partner or both partners are having extra-marital affairs. It is breaking the marital vows. This has deprived many homes the joy and blessings they should derive from marriage. Some partners, especially men see it as a thing of pride to keep marital affairs while some, especially women see it as a way to make extra money to augment what they have. It is an unholy act and irritating to God (Gal 5:19).
LESSON OUTLINES
DANGERS OF UNFAITHFULNESS IN MARRIAGE
It hinders answers to prayers, God does not answer the prayer of a sinner (John 9:31).
It makes it difficult to trust each other again.
It causes spiritual damage (Gen 3:8-10, I Cor 6:18-20)
It makes partners lose interest in each other, therefore creating communication gap.
It affects the cheated partner and children emotionally.
It makes you lose dignity and respect (Proverbs 5:9)
There are chances of contacting sexually transmitted disease.
Your labour will be eaten by another person (Proverbs 5:10)
It always lead to regret (Proverbs 5:11-12)
It leads to hell fire (I Cor 6:9-10)
BE WATCHFUL
In most cases, causes of infidelity are attractive dressing from opposite gender, closeness to another opposite gender, carelessness and worldliness. As Christian, we have to be careful;
Avoid unnecessary closeness to another man or woman
Partners should dress attractively to their partners.
Avoid every appearances of evil - I Thess 5:22
Avoid communication that does not please God (unpleasant jokes).
Let there be boundaries between you and opposite gender.
Be prayerful, so that you would not fall into temptation.
LIFE APPLICATION
Maintain your marital promises to your partner, let your home give glory to God and be referred to positively.

title: IBAWI
memory_verse: Gbogbo ibawi ko dabi ohun ayo nisisiyi, bikose ibanuje; sugbon nikehin a so alafia fun awon ti a ti to nipa re, ani eso ododo.
introduction: Ibawi je titako iwa ti eniyan wu pelu ijeniya. O je ona ti ona ti o ma ndun eniyan ti Olorun ma fi to awon omo ti o ba se lodi pada sinu ife re. Gegebi awon obi ninu aye se ma n ba omo won wi pelu ife nitori won fe rere fun omo na, ero Olorun na ni lati ba wa wi fun rere wa. O tunmo si wipe a je ti Olorun. Ibawi ma nwa nitori ife, ki i se nitori ikorira tabi lati wu iwa ika. O ma n bi iwa bi Olorun, irele ati oye.
lesson_aim: Ibawi je ona lati mu wa pada si ife Olorun, ki i se lati wu iwa ika
application: Gba ibawi lati owo Olorun, ki ibasepo iwo ati Olorun le pada bo si ipo, wa si di alagbara ninu emi si.

BIBELI KIKA: Heberu 12:4-11
ORO AKOSO
Ibawi je titako iwa ti eniyan wu pelu ijeniya. O je ona ti ona ti o ma ndun eniyan ti Olorun ma fi to awon omo ti o ba se lodi pada sinu ife re. Gegebi awon obi ninu aye se ma n ba omo won wi pelu ife nitori won fe rere fun omo na, ero Olorun na ni lati ba wa wi fun rere wa. O tunmo si wipe a je ti Olorun. Ibawi ma nwa nitori ife, ki i se nitori ikorira tabi lati wu iwa ika. O ma n bi iwa bi Olorun, irele ati oye.
PINPIN EKO
IDI FUN IBAWI
Awon idi fun ibawi niyi;
Lati fi ese wa han, ki a si yipada.
Lati mu ibasepo wa pelu Olorun bo si ipo.
Lati jeki a tunbo je olooto
Lati re wa sile
Lati ko wa bi ati nwa ni isora/ikiyesara nipa ti emi
Lati mura wa sile fun ise si.
ONA TI OLORUN MA GBA BA AWON OMO RE WI
Aini ibale okan tabi wahala, ki a le pada si eto Olorun- Jona 1:1-17
Olrun ba Dafidi wi fun ese re â II Sam 12:1-14
Olorun ba Jakobu wi nigbati o n sin ni Labani â Gen 31:38-41
Olorun ba awon omo Israeli wi ni gbogbo irin ajo won â Lef 26:27-28
Olorun le lo awon eniyan lati fib a awon omo re wi â Joshua 7:1-12
Olorun le lo aisan, aini, pipadanu awon oun rere lati fi ba awon omo re wi
SA FUN IWA TI KO TO
Ni asiko ibawi, mase wu iwa ti ko to. Gba ibawi na, ki o si gba ti awon ti o gba o ni imoran pe ki o kuro ninu ijo tabi ki o tako ibawi na. Ibawi je apere pe Olorun feran re. ibawi je on ape Olorun nsise ninu re, o si njeri pe Oun feran re. O je ona ti Olorun ngba sise lori aye re, ki o le jade gegebi asegun, wa si lagbara si ninu emi.
LILO EKA NA
Gba ibawi lati owo Olorun, ki ibasepo iwo ati Olorun le pada bo si ipo, wa si di alagbara ninu emi si.

title: CHASTISEMENT
memory_verse: Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.
introduction: Chastisement is strong rebuke combined with punishment. It is a painful process in which God corrects His rebellious children to go back to His will. Just as earthly parents correct their children out of love for their own good, Godâs intention in correcting us is for our good. It is a proof that we belong to God. Chastisement is about love and not wickedness. It leads to godliness, humility and wisdom.
lesson_aim: Chastisement is to correct us back to the will of God and not an act of wickedness
application: Embrace the discipline from God so that your relationship can be restored and you would become stronger spiritually.
raw_text:
TOPIC: CHASTISEMENT
AIM: Chastisement is to correct us back to the will of God and not an act of wickedness
MEMORY VERSE: Hebrews 12:11; Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.
BIBLE PASSAGE: Hebrews 12:4-11
INTRODUCTION
Chastisement is strong rebuke combined with punishment. It is a painful process in which God corrects His rebellious children to go back to His will. Just as earthly parents correct their children out of love for their own good, Godâs intention in correcting us is for our good. It is a proof that we belong to God. Chastisement is about love and not wickedness. It leads to godliness, humility and wisdom.
LESSON OUTLINES
PURPOSE OF CHASTISEMENT
The purpose of chastisement are;
To reveal your sin and lead you to repentance.
To restore your fellowship with God.
To make you become more faithful
To keep you humble
To teach you spiritual discernment
To prepare you for more effective service.
HOW GOD CHASTISES HIS CHILDREN
Unrest to correct us to His plan- Jonah 1:1-17
God chastised David for his sin â II Sam 12:1-14
God punished Jacob while serving at Labanâs house â Gen 31:38-41
God chastised the Israelites throughout their journey â Lev 26:27-28
God can use men to punish His Children â Joshua 7:1-12
God can use sickness, poverty, loss of good things to chastise his Children
AVOID NEGATIVE ATTITUDE
During chastisement, do not put on a negative attitude. Embrace the discipline and do not give ear to people suggesting that you should leave the church or revolt. Chastisement is a sign that God loves you. Chastisement is God working in you and proving that He loves you. It is a way of God investing in you, so that you can come out victorious and spiritually stronger.
LESSON APPLICATION
Embrace the discipline from God so that your relationship can be restored and you would become stronger spiritually.

title: THE SECOND COMING OF CHRIST

introduction: Jesus gave us signs that will precede His second coming (Matthew 24) and Apostles Paul encouraged the brethren about the fate of the dead in Christ (I Thess 4:13-18). lesson_aim: To learn the signs and events at the second coming of Christ and how to prepare for it.
application: The essence of coming to church, enduring suffering and living holy is to reign with Christ, do not allow anything to hinder you from getting to heaven.

title: IRETI AWON OLODOD

application: Mase je ki irora asiko yi gba ijoba orun ni owo re, irora na o ni pe tan, a o si ogo na han.

ORO AKOSO
Igbe wa ni ibi gbogbo lori oro aje ti ko dara. Ko si orileede ti o yo kale kuro ninu wahal yi. Gbogbo nkan won, iye ti a nra ounje ati a nse ise ko rorun mo. Aisi abo tun wa mu ki gbogbo re o buru si, ati olowo ati talaka ni ko yo kale. Ijoba nfi kun owo ori ki owo le wole fun awon, won o si se nkankan silu pada. Ko si ikunpa lodo ijoba mo. Eleyi je igbe gbogbo eniyan, se ona abayo ma wa? Nje a ma bo?
PINPIN EKO
AWA NINU IGBEKUN: Romu 8:22-23
Nkan le nibi gbogbo, ko si ibi ti a le sa si. Gbogbo aye je igbekun, ko si bi a se le sa kuro ninu aye yi, laise pe iku ba pa eniyan, ese si ni ti eniyan ba pa ara re. Awon miran je alailera, won si nje irora. Awon miran o mo ona ti won o se ri ounje je. O dabi enipe a wa ninu kuku, esu lo ndari aye (1 John 5:19).
IRETI AWON OLODODO:
A nfojusona si ile ologo, ibi ti Olorun ti pese fun wa. E jeki a foriti die si, ki a si ma fi suru reti ileri Olorun na (Heb 13:14, Heb 11:16). Ipenija na le po si, duro lori igbagbo re, ki o si di nkan ti o gbagbo mu. A o ni pe bo lowo irora, a o si fi ogo na han laipe (Heb 11:10-16).
LILO EKO NA
Mase je ki irora asiko yi gba ijoba orun ni owo re, irora na o ni pe tan, a o si ogo na han.

lesson_aim: The only hope for the righteous is the assurance of the everlasting life
application: Do not let the present pain take away heaven from you, the pain will soon be over and the glory shall be revealed.
raw_text:
TOPIC: HOPE OF THE RIGHTEOUS
AIM: The only hope for the righteous is the assurance of the everlasting life
MEMORY VERSE: Philippians 3:20; For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ.
BIBLE PASSAGE: Romans 8:18-19
INTRODUCTION
There are cry everywhere about economic hardship. No country is exempted from this problem. There is inflation, prices of food and services are no longer affordable. Insecurity makes the problem worse, both the rich and poor are not spared. Government is increasing taxes to get more revenue without giving back to the economy. There is no subsidy again. These are the cries of the masses. Will there be a way forward? Will there be a breakthrough?
LESSON OUTLINES
WE ARE IN BONDAGE: Romans 8:22-23
Things are hard everywhere, so there is nowhere to run to. The whole world is a bondage, there is no way out of this world, except death kills a person and it is a sin commit suicide. Some people are weak in health and are in pain. Some do not know where their next meal is coming from. It is as if we are in a nest, devil controls the world (1 John 5:19).
THE HOPE OF THE RIGHTEOUS:
We are looking forward to a glorious home, a place prepared for us by God. We should endure more and be patiently waiting for the promise of God (Heb 13:14, Heb 11:16). The challenge may become more severe, maintain your faith, and hold unto what you believe. We shall soon be free from pain, the glory shall be revealed soon (Heb 11:10-16).
LESSON APPLICATION
Do not let the present pain take away heaven from you, the pain will soon be over and the glory shall be revealed.

lesson_aim: To learn lessons from the birth of Jesus and let others know about Christ

raw_text:
TOPIC: CHRISTMAS
AIM:  To learn lessons from the birth of Jesus and let others know about Christ
MEMORY VERSE: Isaiah 9:6; For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called wonderful, counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.
BIBLE PASSAGE: Luke 2:1-40
INTRODUCTION
Another Christmas is here, you might have planned for clothes, food, drinks and visitations. If you plan for all these without knowing Christ, you celebration is a waste. What is your plan about knowing Christ? Or what is your plan for Christ in this Christmas period? If you have known Christ, what is your plan about telling others the purpose of the birth of Jesus Christ? Will you just merry around and not think about the plan of God for you and others?
LESSON OUTLINES
LESSONS IN THE BIRTH OF JESUS:
Jesus was born in the manger. Our Lord is humble, we should show humility in all we are doing.
During Jesusâ birth, there was an instruction that everyone should register his/her name at his/her native land (census), His parent obeyed the instruction. They are responsible citizens.
The wise men saw the sign and they did not keep quiet, they shared the good news as they went to see the new born king (Matteu 2:1-7).
Christmas shows the love of God to mankind without any discrimination. We should love everyone irrespective of tribe or religion.
God loves us despite our sin. We should not cut our relationship with other because they offend us. We should learn to forgive.
WHAT WE SHOULD DO DURING CHRISTMAS:
Christmas is the time to review our relationship with God. Has the purpose of the birth of Christ being achieved in your life?
It is the time to let others know about Christ.
It is the time to show love to people (less privilege, the poor, widows, orphan etc.)
LESSON APPLICATION
Spread the good news during this Christmas by explaining the purpose of the birth of Jesus to people.

title: IWALAYE OLORUN
memory_verse: Nitori ohun re ti o farasin lati igba dida aiye a ri won gbangba, a nfi oye ohun ti a da mo o, ani agbara ati iwa-Olorun re ayeraiye, ki nwon ki o le wa li airiwi
introduction: Ni opolopo igba, a ma ri ibere bi Nje Olorun wa? Bawo ni o se ri? Se o le se apejuwe bi o se ri? Ti o ba le ro lati fi eri han nipa iwalaye Olorun, awon eniyan ma nfe oun ti o se fi oju ri ti o fi eri han pe Olorun wa. Bibeli ti fi han fun ni awon ona pupo pe Olorun wa.

AKOSORI: Romu 1:20; Nitori ohun re ti o farasin lati igba dida aiye a ri won gbangba, a nfi oye ohun ti a da mo o, ani agbara ati iwa-Olorun re ayeraiye, ki nwon ki o le wa li airiwi
BIBELI KIKA: Orin Dafidi 14:1-5
ORO AKOSO
Ni opolopo igba, a ma ri ibere bi Nje Olorun wa? Bawo ni o se ri? Se o le se apejuwe bi o se ri? Ti o ba le ro lati fi eri han nipa iwalaye Olorun, awon eniyan ma nfe oun ti o se fi oju ri ti o fi eri han pe Olorun wa. Bibeli ti fi han fun ni awon ona pupo pe Olorun wa.
PINPIN EKO
AWON ERI TI O FIHAN PE OLORUN WA
Iseda â Ti iseda ba wa, eyi ni awon oun ti a da, eleda won gbodo wa. - Rom 1:20, Job 37:7, Isaiah 40:25-26, Orin Daf 19:1, Oniwasu 3:11.
Itoleseese wa fun gbogbo oun ti a da â Orun o ni jade ni ale, be si ni osupa ko ni jade ni osan. Ikookan won ni o ni ala ti a ti la kale fun â Owe 8:23-29, Job 37:7-13, Gen 1:1-31. Tani o seto awon eto ati Ilakale wonyi?
Olorun ma nba awon omo re soro â Heb 1:1-2, Job 33:14-18
O nfun ni ni emi, o si ma n gba - Oniwasu 8:8, Matt 6:27.
Eri Okan eniyan â Eni kookan ni o mo ohun ti o to ati oun ti ko to lati igba ewe. Tani o ko won lati igba ewe won? Romu 2:14-15.
Awon ise iyanu Olorun
IGBAGBO
Gbi gbagbo bere pelu gbigba pe Olorun wa. Ko si eni ti o ri Olorun re (Johanu 1:18), sugbon a mo pe o wa nipa awon eri ti a toka si yi. Igbagbo je ijeri si oun ti a ko ri. Igbagbo wa nipa gbigbo, ki i se nipa riri (Rom 10:17) ati pe ibukun ni fun awon ti ko ri Olorun ti won si gbagbo (John 20:24-29). Ninu ibasepo wa pelu Olorun, o gbodo gbagbo ninu Jesu pe;
Pe omo Olorun ni â Johanu 3:16
Pe Oun ni ona, otito ati iye - Johanu 14:6
Oun ni etutu fun iwenumo ese â Heberu 9:12-22
Pe Oun ni Oluwa, ki o si gbagbo ninu metalokan â Heberu 1:1-4
Pe Oun ni yio se idajo aye â Ise Aposteli 17:31, Mateu 25:31-46
LILO EKO NA FUN AYE WA
O le gbe igbe aye re bi o ti wu o. Olorun ni o fun o ni emi inu re, wa si jihin gbogbo ohun ti o ba se fun un. Eni je ojo ti o dara lati seto ibalaje larin iwo ati Olorun.

title: THE EXISTENCE OF GOD
memory_verse: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse.
introduction: Many times, we have come across questions like does God exist? How does He/She looks like? Can you describe Him/Her? If you think of proving Godâs existence, people want something physical to prove that God actually exists. The Bible has revealed to us in many ways that God exists.
lesson_aim: To show proofs that God exists.
application: You cannot just live your life the way you like it. God gave you the life and you will give account of everything you do to him. Today is the best time to reconcile with God.
raw_text:
TOPIC: THE EXISTENCE OF GOD
AIM: To show proofs that God exists.
MEMORY VERSE: Romans 1:20; For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse.
BIBLE PASSAGE: Psalms 14:1-5
INTRODUCTION
Many times, we have come across questions like does God exist? How does He/She looks like? Can you describe Him/Her? If you think of proving Godâs existence, people want something physical to prove that God actually exists. The Bible has revealed to us in many ways that God exists.
LESSON OUTLINES
PROOFS THAT GOD EXIST
Creature â If there is creature, there must be a creator - Rom 1:20, Job 37:7, Isaiah 40:25-26, Psalms 19:1, Eccl 3:11.
There is orderliness in all the things created â the sun would not come out in the night, neither would the moon show up in the day. They have their boundaries â Prov 8:23-29, Job 37:7-13, Gen 1:1-31. Who made these arrangement/instructions?
He communicates with his children â Hebrew 1:1-2, Job 33:14-18
He gives and takes life- Eccl 8:8, Matt 6:27.
Human conscience â For every man knows what is right from wrong since the period of childhood. Who taught them from childhood? Romans 2:14-15.
His miracles -
FAITH
Believing starts with accepting God that He exists. No one has seen God (John 1:18) but we believe He exists because of the points highlighted above. Faith is the evidence of things not seeing. Faith comes by hearing, not by seeing (Rom 10:17) and blessed are they that believe without seeing God (John 20:24-29). In the journey of a relationship with God, you must believe in Jesus Christ;
As the son of God â John 3:16
As the way, the truth and the life - John 14:6
As the only sacrifice for the remission â Hebrew 9:12-22
As the Lord, and in the trinity â Heb 1:1-4
As the person to judge the world â Acts 17:31, Matthew 25:31-46
LIFE APPLICATION
You cannot just live your life the way you like it. God gave you the life and you will give account of everything you do to him. Today is the best time to reconcile with God.

title: CONFORMING WITH THE WORLD
memory_verse: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.
introduction: Worldliness is thinking and behaving like unbelievers do and deriving pleasures from what God has warned us against. Worldliness embraces devilish and seductive acts. Conforming with the world is a total inconsistent to the things of God.
lesson_aim: To guard ourselves against worldliness
application:
HOW DOES THE WORLD PRESSURE US TO CONFORM
Isolation
Intimidation/persecution
Indoctrination
WAYS CHRISTIANS CONFORM WITH THE WORLD
Entertainment
Education (choosing wrong mentor)
Friendship
Business
fashion
CAREFULNESS:
We conform gradually through carelessness, not paying attention to the purpose and means of things introduce to us. The understanding of what is the purpose of things introduced to us or understanding the ways in achieving some things will save us from worldliness. We should ask questions like will God be pleased with the means I achieved this goal or will God be happy with this way of life.
Understand that not everything introduced to you is acceptable, weigh them on biblical instructions.

Olorun wa wa nibi gbogbo. Dafidi se alaye wipe ko si eniti o sa kuro lodo Olorun. Ti o ba wa ni oju ofurufu, labe omi, ninu iho apata, ninu ile, o wa nibe. Oju Oluwa wa nibi gbogbo (Owe 15:3, Jer 23:23-24, Heb 4:13, Ise Aposteli 17:27), nitorina gbogbo oun ti o ba nse nibikibi ni Olorun mo.

title: SECRET SIN
memory_verse: Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? Saith the LORD. Do not I fill heaven and earth? Saith the LORD.
introduction: Secret sins are behaviours not in accordance to the will of God, the atrocities and wickedness carried out when no other person was present. The sinner left no traces in which the offence, wickedness or evil could be linked to him. The sinner felt he/she has avoided the consequences of the evil committed. Some people kidnapped, stole, killed, raped or hypnotized the other secretly and no other person know the person behind all that happened, they forget that if no man sees them, the God in heaven sees all.
lesson_aim: To let you know that what you call secret sin is not secret.
application: No sin is secret. It may be hidden to men, but it is not hidden to God. It is better to confess all secret sins now than to be revealed on the day of judgement.
raw_text:
TOPIC: SECRET SIN
AIM: To let you know that what you call secret sin is not secret.
MEMORY VERSE: Jeremiah 23:24; Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? Saith the LORD. Do not I fill heaven and earth? Saith the LORD.
BIBLE PASSAGE: Psalms 139:7-13
INTRODUCTION
Secret sins are behaviours not in accordance to the will of God, the atrocities and wickedness carried out when no other person was present. The sinner left no traces in which the offence, wickedness or evil could be linked to him. The sinner felt he/she has avoided the consequences of the evil committed. Some people kidnapped, stole, killed, raped or hypnotized the other secretly and no other person know the person behind all that happened, they forget that if no man sees them, the God in heaven sees all.
LESSON OUTLINES
THE OMNIPRESENCE OF GOD
Our God is everywhere. David described that nobody could run away from God. if you are in the sky, under the water, in the cave, under the ground He is present there.  The eyes of the Lord are in every place (Prov 15:3, Jer 23:23-24, Heb 4:13, Acts 17:27), therefore everything you do anywhere is known to Him
NO SIN IS HIDDEN
Example of people whose secret sins were exposed;
Achan â Joshua 7:1-25
Cain â Gen 4:9-10
Gehazi â II Kings 5:20-27
Ananias and Sapphira â Acts 5:1-11
Judas Iscariot â Matthew 26:20-25, John 13:24-28
CONFESS YOUR SINS
It is better for your sins to be exposed now and reconcile with God than your sin to be hidden and revealed later on the judgement day when forgiveness of the sin would not be available - I Tim 5:24. Confess your sin to God and seek His forgiveness. There is still grace for forgiveness of sins.
LIFE APPLICATION
No sin is secret. It may be hidden to men, but it is not hidden to God. It is better to confess all secret sins now than to be revealed on the day of judgement.

title: FAITHFUL SERVANT

AKORI EKO: OLOOTO IRANSE
ERONGBA: Jije olooto ma farahan nipa bi a Gbekele le o si.
AKOSORI: I Korinti 4:2; Pelupelu a mbere lowo iriju pe ki oluware na ki o je oloto.
BIBELI KIKA: Matteu 24:45-50
ORO AKOSO
Ije olooto ni fifi atileyin otito ati igba de igba han, eniyan se gbarale, o si na mu ileri re se ati ki a ojuse wa ni igba ti o ye ki a se. Gegebi Kristeni, a je iranse Olorun, gbogbo wa ni a pe si ise ihinrere. Ati pe gegebi osise, igbalero awon eniyan nipe ati mo Olorun daradara, a si ti fun wa ni ojuse miran yato si ipe lati gba aye la, a si mo awon nkan ti o ye ki a se ni igba de igba fun itankale ihinrere ati idagbasoke ise iranse.
PINPIN EKO
KINI JIJE OLOOTO TUMO SI? Jije olooto ni ki eniyan je;
Eniti o duro sinsin
Olufokansin
Eniti o se gbarale
Eniti o fi ara ji si ife Olorun ati ileri re.
APEJUWE AWON TI O JE OLOOTO IRANSE
Olooto Iranse je eniti ti o le isakoso bi o ti to. Yio lo isura bi o ti to (Iba je eniyan tabi nkan miran) â Luku 16:11-12; Luku 19:17. Eniyan je isura Olorun ti o tobi ju, a gbodo lo se isakoso won daradara (Matteu 18:11-14).
Olooto iranse ki i se se-ka-ri-mi, ti awon eniyan npe ni oju aye. Ki i se alagabangebe.  â Gal 2:11-14
Olooto iranse mo bi akoko se se pataki si. O ma se ise ni kiakia (gegebi eniti ojuse se pataki fun ise isin, ko ye ki a sese ma so fun o ki o to se ojuse re) Fun bi apere; Akorin, adena, awon ti o nbojuto ero agbohun, Oluko ileeko ojo isinmi ati awon miran. Olooto iranse gbodo ni afojusun.
O gbekele agbara Olorun â Eph 3:7
O je eniti o se ko ni eko
O ma yonda ara re fun ise. Oni ifara-eni-ji si oun ti Olorun ati ijo (O ma wa sile ijosin deede)
O ni suuru
Olooto iranse ma nmu ileri re se.
O ma fi ti enikeji saaju
O ni iwabi-Olorun.
LILO EKO NA
Okan lara ona lati mo bi o se je olooto si ni bi awon eniyan se le gbarale o si, se adari re le gbarale o.

title: OLOOTO IRANSE (APA KEJI)
memory_verse: Oluwa si so fun Satani pe, Iwo ha kiyesi Jobu iranse mi, pe, ko si ekeji re li aiye, okunrin ti ise oloto, ti o si duro sinsin, eniti o beâru Olorun, ti o si korira iwa buburu.
introduction:
Idurosisnsin ni wiwu iwa gegebi ati mo o, ni igba ti awon ti o mo ko si ni ayika re. O je diduro lori ijewo igbagbo re. Idurosinsin ni ifesemule lori awon ilana igbagbo, aiyese nigba ipenija ati didagba ninu awon eto Olorun fun wa lati dabi Kristi. Ni kukuru, o tumo si;
Didi igbagbo mu
Gbigbekele Olorun ninu idanwo
Kiko lati dabi Kristi
Awon ijo akoko fi idurosinsin won han nipa diduro lori awon nkan ti won ti ko lehin ti won ti ya ara awon  (Ise Aposteli 8:1-5).
lesson_aim: Lati ko nipa iduro sinsin ati awon anfani ti o wa ninu jije Olooto
application: A o dan ijolooto re wo, ri wipe o duro sinsin. Ere wa fun un. .
raw_text:
AKORI EKO: OLOOTO IRANSE (APA KEJI)
ERONGBA: Lati ko nipa iduro sinsin ati awon anfani ti o wa ninu jije Olooto
AKOSORI: Jobu 1:8; Oluwa si so fun Satani pe, Iwo ha kiyesi Jobu iranse mi, pe, ko si ekeji re li aiye, okunrin ti ise oloto, ti o si duro sinsin, eniti o beâru Olorun, ti o si korira iwa buburu.
BIBELI KIKA: Matteu 25:14-29
ORO AKOSO
Idurosisnsin ni wiwu iwa gegebi ati mo o, ni igba ti awon ti o mo ko si ni ayika re. O je diduro lori ijewo igbagbo re. Idurosinsin ni ifesemule lori awon ilana igbagbo, aiyese nigba ipenija ati didagba ninu awon eto Olorun fun wa lati dabi Kristi. Ni kukuru, o tumo si;
Didi igbagbo mu
Gbigbekele Olorun ninu idanwo
Kiko lati dabi Kristi
Awon ijo akoko fi idurosinsin won han nipa diduro lori awon nkan ti won ti ko lehin ti won ti ya ara awon  (Ise Aposteli 8:1-5).
PINPIN EKO
IDUROSINSIN: Bibeli kika wa fihan wipe awon iranse fi ara won ji si ise won, won si gba ere fun. Ise Jesu ni aye ni iwasu ihinrere; a pe wa lati jere okan fun Kristi (Matteu 28:18-19), ki a si ko won ki won gbe igbeaye won gegebi eko Kristi. A ri eko ko lara Jobu ati Paulu, won gbekele Olorun ninu idanwo won (Job 1:22, I Kor ). Dafidi fi tokantokan sin saulu, bo tele je wipe Saulu o feran re. Ifokansin yi mu ki Saulu gbekele (I Sam 18:3; 19:4). O gbodo ni idurosinsin ninu igbagbo (Juda 1:3-4, Kol 2:5-7, II Kor 11:3-4, II Pet 3:14-18), ninu ise iranse (Ise Aposteli 6:4), ninu siso otito (Matt 23:27-28) ati ninu ise re (Filipi 3:8-9, I Kor 10:23).
ANFANI TI O NINU JIJE OLOOTO:
Alafia ati itelorun â Fil 4:6-7
Jije olooto ma nmu iyi wa â Heb 6:10, Jobu 42:11
O ma nfun eniyan ni ireti â Jer 29:11; Gal 6:9
O ma nmu aseyori wa â Jobu 42:12
O ma nmu ki igbagbo eniyan ki dagba
Eso tie mi ma npo si
Awon olooto ni yio jogun ijoba orun â Matteu 25:21
O ma fun eniyan ni eri okan ti o mo â II Kor 1:12
O ma fun eniyan ni abo lati odo Olorun â Owe 6:16, II Thess 3:3, Orin Dafidi 31:23
O ma fun eniyan ni ipese ati odo Olorun wa â Owe 28: 20
LILO EKO NA
A o dan ijolooto re wo, ri wipe o duro sinsin. Ere wa fun un. .

title: FAITHFUL SERVANT II
memory_verse: And the Lord said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil?
introduction:
Steadfastness is professing what you are known for in the absence of those who know you. It is maintaining your declaration of faith. Steadfastness is holding firm to the principle of faith, standing on your ground in challenges and growing through the processes of becoming like Christ. In short, it means;
Holding unto faith
Trusting God in trials
Learning to become like Christ (Discipleship).
The early church displayed steadfastness by holding unto what they have learned after they separated (Act 8:1-5).
lesson_aim: To learn about steadfastness and the benefits in being faithful
application: Your faithfulness will be tested, try to maintain your steadfastness. There is reward for it.
raw_text:
TOPIC: FAITHFUL SERVANT II
AIM: To learn about steadfastness and the benefits in being faithful
MEMORY VERSE: Job 1:8; And the Lord said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil?
BIBLE PASSAGE:	Matthew 25:14-29
INTRODUCTION
Steadfastness is professing what you are known for in the absence of those who know you. It is maintaining your declaration of faith. Steadfastness is holding firm to the principle of faith, standing on your ground in challenges and growing through the processes of becoming like Christ. In short, it means;
Holding unto faith
Trusting God in trials
Learning to become like Christ (Discipleship).
The early church displayed steadfastness by holding unto what they have learned after they separated (Act 8:1-5).
LESSON OUTLINES
STEADFASTNESS: The bible passage shows that some servants were committed to their profession and they got reward for it. The business of Jesus on earth is evangelism; we have been called to win souls for Christ (Matthew 28:18-19) and teach them to live by the teaching of Christ. We also learnt from Job and Paul, they trusted God in their trials (Job 1:22, I Cor ). David was committed and loyal in his duty despite being hated by Saul and this made Saul to trust him (I Sam 18:3; 19:4). You must be steadfast in your faith (Jude 1:3-4, Col 2:5-7, II Cor 11:3-4, II Pet 3:14-18), in ministry (Acts 6:4), in saying the truth (Matt 23:27-28) and in your work (Philip 3:8-9, I Cor 10:23).
BENEFITS OF FAITHFULNESS:
Peace and contentment â Phil 4:6-7
Faithfulness bring honour â Heb 6:10, Job 42:11
It gives hope â Jer 29:11; Gal 6:9
It brings fulfilment â Job 42:12
Faithfulness develops your faith
The fruit of the spirit abound
Faithful people will inherit the kingdom of God â Mtthew 25:21
It gives a clear conscience â II Cor 1:12
It brings divine protection â Prov 6:16, II Thess 3:3, Paslms 31:23
It brings divine provision â Prov 28: 20
LIFE APPLICATION
Your faithfulness will be tested, try to maintain your steadfastness. There is reward for it.

title: GODLINESS
memory_verse: This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.
introduction: Godliness means behaving like Jesus. It implies asking yourself, what would Jesus would have done in this situation? People are acting holy now, they are not living holy. We are religious, we are not righteous. On Sunday, the church would be filled to the brim with people claiming to be lifting up holy hands, among them are drug dealers, adulterers, backbiters, gossipers, promise breakers, cheaters and manipulators.
lesson_aim: Godliness is not about being religious, it is being righteousness.
application: Stop pretending to be godly, let your true behaviour be known to people.
raw_text:
TOPIC: GODLINESS
AIM: Godliness is not about being religious, it is being righteousness.
MEMORY VERSE: Matthew 15:8; This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.
BIBLE PASSAGE: Isaiah 29:13
INTRODUCTION
Godliness means behaving like Jesus. It implies asking yourself, what would Jesus would have done in this situation? People are acting holy now, they are not living holy. We are religious, we are not righteous. On Sunday, the church would be filled to the brim with people claiming to be lifting up holy hands, among them are drug dealers, adulterers, backbiters, gossipers, promise breakers, cheaters and manipulators.
LESSON OUTLINES
ACT OF GODLINESS: Godliness is a word that summarises the way a person who lives according to Christ behaves. So as Christ lived, a godly person must;
forgive â Matt 6:14-15, Matt 18:21-35
purity of heart â John 1:47
show genuine love â I John 3:16-18, Eph 5:2
Goodness â James 1:27, Eph 5:9
Confession of sin â James 5:16
Tolerance â Col 3:12-13
Humility/meekness â Matt 18:4; Eph 5:21
Truthful â Eph 4:24-28
DEPART FROM EVIL COMPANY:
In order to live a godly live, your companions must be godly. Your company influences your behaviour. God warned the Israelites not to seek help from the ungodly nations â Isaiah 31:1, He warned them not to marry from the nations Deut 7:3, Deut 23:3. Being associated with unbelievers is being unequally yoked II Cor 6:14, I Cor 15:33. We should move in the company of people that would help our faith and make living a holy life easy for us â Heb 10:25.
LIFE APPLICATION
Stop pretending to be godly, let your true behaviour be known to people.

title: IWA BI OLORUN
memory_verse: Awon enia yi nfi enu won sunmo mi, nwon si nfi ete won bola fun mi; sugbon okan won jina si mi.
introduction: Iwa-bi-Olorun je wiwu iwa bi Jesu. O tumo bibere lowo ara wa pe bawo ni Jesu o ba se wuwa ni iru ikorita yi? Awon eniyan se afarawe iwa mimo sugbon won o gbe igbeaye iwa mimo. A je elesin, sugbon a ki n se olododo. Ni Ojo isinmi, ile ijosin o kun fun awon eniyan ti won so wipe awon gbe owo mimo soke, lara won ni awon ologun oloro, alagbere, abatenije, olofofo, eletan, arenije ati alailoto.
lesson_aim: Iwa bi Olorun ki se pe ki eniyan je elesin, sugbon o je jije Olododo.
application: Ye ma wuwa agabangebe bi eniti o nhuwa bi Olorun, jeki awon eniyan mo iwa re gangan.

Dariji â Matt 6:14-15, Matt 18:21-35

Isoore â Jakobu 1:27, Efe 5:9

title: VOW
memory_verse: I will pay my vows unto the LORD now in the presence of all his people.
introduction:
Vow is a promise to do something. Either you are playing or not, the person would be expecting what you have promised. Whoever vowed in the presence of the Lord and did not redeem is regarded as a fool â Eccl 5:4
You cannot cancel a vow and say it is an error â Eccl 5:6, Judges 11:35
Promise is a debt, we are urge not to owe anyone â Romans 13:8
The Lord will require it from you, it will become a sin â Deut 23:21
Failure to pay your vow can make God to destroy the work of your hand â Eccl 5:6

Promise to praise God â Psalm 65:1
Promise to give a substance to God â Judges 11:39, Jonah 2:9
All promises to the Church
Promises to serve the church as a worker
Monetary promises
All promises to man
Marital vows â Mal 2:14-15
Promise to pay debt

Promise to serve others

title: FORGIVENESS
memory_verse: Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive and ye shall be forgiven
introduction: Forgiveness is to end anger or bitterness towards a person for an offence. It to overlook resentment and the pain we planned to inflict on the person that hurt us. Forgiveness is not theoretical, it is what to be done. We are in the world where people want to prove what/who is right or wrong and wants to revenge. To Christians, forgiveness is not selective or partial. It is a must because we have been forgiven also (Romans 5:8).
lesson_aim: We are to forgive in order to have our sins forgiven
application: Forgiveness may seem difficult because of the gravity of the offence, but we are commanded to forgive irrespective of the offence. Pray to God to soften your heart and lead you through the process of forgiveness.
raw_text:
TOPIC: FORGIVENESS
AIM: We are to forgive in order to have our sins forgiven
MEMORY VERSE: Luke 6:37; Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive and ye shall be forgiven
BIBLE PASSAGE: Matthew 18:21-34
INTRODUCTION
Forgiveness is to end anger or bitterness towards a person for an offence. It to overlook resentment and the pain we planned to inflict on the person that hurt us. Forgiveness is not theoretical, it is what to be done. We are in the world where people want to prove what/who is right or wrong and wants to revenge. To Christians, forgiveness is not selective or partial. It is a must because we have been forgiven also (Romans 5:8).
LESSON OUTLINES
FACTS ABOUT FORGIVENESS
It is a command â Col 3:13.
It is choice and a decision to be made.
Forgiveness is for all offences, it is not selective. No sin is unforgiveable.
Forgiveness is not conditional â Luke 23:34
Forgiveness allows God to be the judge, and He will fight for you â Romans 12:19-21
Unforgiveness hinders prayer â Mark 11:25-26
BENEFITS OF FORGIVENESS
Forgiveness makes God to forgive your sin âMatthew 6:14-15, Mark 11-25
Forgiveness connects us deeply with God. We would understand the sacrifice Jesus made for us on the cross better. We would  understand mercy and you are becoming like Jesus â Eph 4:32
Forgiveness reduces your mental and emotional stress. Holding grudges affects your health. When you forgive, you reduce the heavy burden on your health. You get rid of negative thoughts. â Prov. 27:3
It will restore relationships â Prov 17:9
It hinders the devil from taking advantage of you â II Cor 2:10-11
It brings peace
LIFE APPLICATION
Forgiveness may seem difficult because of the gravity of the offence, but we are commanded to forgive irrespective of the offence. Pray to God to soften your heart and lead you through the process of forgiveness.

title: IDARIJI

introduction: Idariji ni ki a fi opin si gbogbo ibinu ati ikoro okan ti ani si eniyan nitori ese ti o se wa. O je fi fi oju fo ikoro okan ati ipalara ti a ti pinu lati se si eniti o se ipalara si wa. Idariji ki ise eko tabi oro inu iwe, sugbon o je oun ti a nilo lati se. a wa ninu aye ti awon eniyan fe ri eri oun ti o to ati ti ko to han, won si fe gbesan. application: Idaraji le dabi wipe o le nitori bi ese ti eniyan se wa se tabi to, sugbon a pa ni dandan fun wa lati dari gbogbo ese ji. Gbadura ki Olorun jeki okan re o ro, ki o si dari re ninu gbogbo eto idariji.

title: WEAPON OF OUR WARFARE
memory_verse: For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds.
introduction: Christianity is about serving God and warfare. We are fighting the host of darkness, principalities and power. Fighting the host of darkness requires being fully equipped for the battle, as we cannot use things of darkness to fight darkness. There are some changes in Christianity in which candles, sacrifices of animals like goat, ram etc, use of fruits like banana, coconut etc, sprinkling of salt and others are used for warfare. Some carry out redemption work by killing or burying goats/ram. This is contrary to the doctrine of Christ and the believes of the early church.
lesson_aim: The weapons of our warfare are not physical
application: You do not need to apply any physical material before your prayer would be answered.
raw_text:
TOPIC: WEAPON OF OUR WARFARE
AIM: The weapons of our warfare are not physical
MEMORY VERSE: II Cor 10:4; For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds.
BIBLE PASSAGE: Ephesian 6:10-18
INTRODUCTION
Christianity is about serving God and warfare. We are fighting the host of darkness, principalities and power. Fighting the host of darkness requires being fully equipped for the battle, as we cannot use things of darkness to fight darkness. There are some changes in Christianity in which candles, sacrifices of animals like goat, ram etc, use of fruits like banana, coconut etc, sprinkling of salt and others are used for warfare. Some carry out redemption work by killing or burying goats/ram. This is contrary to the doctrine of Christ and the believes of the early church.
LESSON OUTLINES
WEAPONS OF OUR WARFARE:
Word of God â You must be equipped with the word of God ( Col 3:16, Eph 6:17, Isaiah 40:8, Matt 4:1-11
The name of Jesus âProv 18:10; Phil 2:9-11
Wisdom of God â Eccl 7:12, Eccl 10:10
Prayer (including praying in tongues) â James 4:7, Luke 10:18-19,  Jude 1:20, Rom 8:26-27
Blood of Jesus â Revelation 12:11, Col 2:14, Hebrew 12:24
Word of Testimonies - Revelation 12:11
GOD HAS IN MANY TIMES CONFOUND THE WISDOM OF MEN WITH HIS SUPERNATURAL WORKS:
Only shout made the wall of Jericho to fall â Joshua 6:12-20
The host of Syria were confounded â II Kings 7:3-8
God used three hundred men to fight a battle â Judges 7:1-25
Jehoshaphat won the Ammonites and Moabites with praises â II Chro 20:15-26
God used ravens to feed Elijah â I Kings 17:4-6
Esther obtained favour through prayer of the saints â Esther 4:15-17, Esther 5:1-8
WEAPON OF OUR WARFARE REQUIRES FAITH
People always want physical things to apply before they believe that their prayer has answered or it will answer. Pray to God and believe that it will be answered. You do not need to burn incense or candles. The prayers of the righteous always perform wonders. Even the use of water, anointing oil and mantle are just extra. Prayer of faith without applying water, anointing oil and mantle is very effective, and God wants us to operate at this level of faith.
LIFE APPLICATION
You do not need to apply any physical material before your prayer would be answered.

title: THE LEVELS OF FAITH
memory_verse: And Apostles said unto the Lord, increase our faith.
introduction: Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen (Heb 11:1). The level of your faith reflects the level of personal conviction and dependence on the power of God. It determines if prayer would be answered or not (James 1:6-8) because God deals with us base on the level of our faith (Rom 12:3). It is our responsibility to continually grow in faith. Just as muscle is build through physical exercises, our spiritual muscle, faith, is built through spiritual exercises.
lesson_aim: Your faith should continually grow
application: It is your responsibility to build your faith

title: A STUMBLING BLOCK
memory_verse: But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.
introduction: A stumbling block means someone hindering the conversion of another to Christ or hindering the growth of another person in Christ. It can mean someone drawing another person into sin.
lesson_aim: To know ways we can unconsciously be a stumbling block to others
application: There is huge curse laid on whoever makes anyone to stumble. Be cautious of the way you live.

INTRODUCTION
A stumbling block means someone hindering the conversion of another to Christ or hindering the growth of another person in Christ. It can mean someone drawing another person into sin.
LESSON OUTLINES
HOW CAN ONE BE A STUMBLING BLOCK
Your character with people (Dishonesty, fighting, unforgiving, gossiping, hatred etc)
Living a controversial life (Hypocrisy) â Hairstyle, clothing, tattoo etc.
Attending a good bible believing church but your attitude and lifestyle did not reflect that.
Watering down the effect of the word of God (After the message discussion)
You can also be a stumbling block when your action is being misinterpreted as sin.
CONSEQUENCES OF BEING A STUMBLING BLOCK
Stumbling others is the devilâs work and opposes Godâs work
Jesus cursed anyone that stumbled others â Matt 18:7
It damages the fellowship of the believers.
It hardens the stumbled and makes them more inclined to sin
It damages the success of the Gospel.
A CAUTIOUS LIFESTYLE
There is a lesson to learn from Apostle to Paul, in I Cor 10:23, not all things that are lawful can edify. We have to learn how to sacrifice some things because of the people of weak faith among us. We should learn how to react, talk and exercise our right in order to edify people around us.
LIFE APPLICATION
There is huge curse laid on whoever makes anyone to stumble. Be cautious of the way you live.

title: GBIGBE NI IBI IKOKO RE

introduction: Ibi ikoko je ibi ti a ti le ba Olorun soro. O le fi okan re han fun Olorun, Olorun na yio si fi asiri re han o. Ibi ikoko ki i se ibi kan ni pato, o le kepe Olorun ni ibi kibi. title: DWELLING IN HIS SECRET PLACE
memory_verse: And the LORD said, Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon a rock.
introduction: A secret place is where you can communicate with God. You can express your feeling and desire to Him and in return, He will reveal His secret to you. A secret place does not really mean a particular location, you can call on God anywhere. In the days of the Old Testament, the secret place of God is the Holiest of the Holies in the Tabernacle (Heb 9:1-8). The glory and majesty of God shone greatly in the place. Moses and the three disciples, (Exo.33:18-23, Exo 34:1-8, Matt 17:1-8) experienced the glory at the secret place of God. When Jesus died on the cross, the veil on the temple torn and everyone has unlimited access to God (Mark 15:37-39, Heb 9:10-15). You do not need a priest to help you hear the will of God.
lesson_aim: There is an unlimited access to reach God personally.
application: The benefits to be enjoyed in the secret place cannot be exhausted or explained accurately, it is better experienced. Develop a close intimacy with God in order to enjoy these benefits.

title: THE ONLY AND TRUE SACRIFICE
memory_verse: And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission
introduction: In the Old Testament, the Israelites offered different sacrifices to God. They offered the burnt, grain, peace, sin and guilt offerings and each has its own specific purpose. Almost all the sacrifices require the shedding of blood (Lev 2:1-16, Lev 4: 1-5, Lev 5: 14-19, Lev 9:1-24, Lev 8:13-15). This continual use of blood is what Jesus cancelled by using His own blood as sacrifice, once and for all.
lesson_aim: The blood of Jesus has settled all, every other sacrifice offered is idolatry
application: The blood of Jesus has settled all. Whatever your past and future may be demanding, it has been settled on the cross through Jesusâ death and resurrection
raw_text:
TOPIC: THE ONLY AND TRUE SACRIFICE
AIM: The blood of Jesus has settled all, every other sacrifice offered is idolatry
MEMORY VERSE: Hebrew 19:22; And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission
BIBLE PASSAGE: Hebrew 9:6-28
INTRODUCTION
In the Old Testament, the Israelites offered different sacrifices to God. They offered the burnt, grain, peace, sin and guilt offerings and each has its own specific purpose. Almost all the sacrifices require the shedding of blood (Lev 2:1-16, Lev 4: 1-5, Lev 5: 14-19, Lev 9:1-24, Lev 8:13-15). This continual use of blood is what Jesus cancelled by using His own blood as sacrifice, once and for all.
LESSON OUTLINES
THE BLOOD OF JESUS:
There are various religious rites in which blood is shed, all these blood cleanse the body and not the soul. The blood of Jesus:
Brings remission of sin â Heb 9:26, Heb 9:12, Heb 10:4
Blood of Jesus sanctified and perfect us â Heb 10:14
Blood f Jesus speaks better things ( it speaks grace) â Heb 12:24, Eph 1:7
Blood of Jesus purges our soul â Heb 9:13-14
Blood of Jesus created access to God â Eph 2:13, Heb 10:19
Blood of Jesus gives us victory â Rev 12:11
RELIGIOUS RITES
The laws in the Old Testament were religious rites purifying the body and not the soul. The peopleâs hearts were not purged of sin. In fact, the yearly practice of killing calf by the priest was a remembrance of sin (Heb 10:3). God said the people only honoured him with their lips, but their heart is far from me (Matt 15:8). The death and resurrection of Jesus cancelled that yearly rite and purge all filthiness in our heart (Heb 10:17-18)
IT IS FINISHED
Do not allow anyone to deceive you with fake doctrine and heresy. Do not pay for goat or calf for redemption or buy dove or drop any sacrifice at the junction. The blood of Jesus has settled all. The death and resurrection of Christ has given us victory over everything, including death. Jesus said it is FINISHED - John 19:30.
LIFE APPLICATION
The blood of Jesus has settled all. Whatever your past and future may be demanding, it has been settled on the cross through Jesusâ death and resurrection

title: JESUS, THE RESURRECTION AND LIFE
memory_verse: But thanks be to God, which giveth us victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
introduction: Easter is the annual remembrance of the death and resurrection of our Lord, Jesus Christ. It is significant to Christian because it is the foundation of our faith and it gave us a reliability of a life after death (I Cor 15:13-19). Jesus died to unite us with God by taking away our sins. Christianity has no stand if resurrection did not happen, we would have suffered in vain and placed our faith in false hope
lesson_aim: The death and resurrection of Jesus gave us hope of eternal life.
application: There is eternal life which has been secured through the death and resurrection of Christ, but you can only have the eternal life by reconciling with your maker. Let the purpose of His resurrection be fulfilled in your life.
raw_text:
TOPIC: JESUS, THE RESURRECTION AND LIFE
AIM: The death and resurrection of Jesus gave us hope of eternal life.
MEMORY VERSE: I Corinthians 15:57; But thanks be to God, which giveth us victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
BIBLE PASSAGE: I Corinthians 15:51-58
INTRODUCTION
Easter is the annual remembrance of the death and resurrection of our Lord, Jesus Christ. It is significant to Christian because it is the foundation of our faith and it gave us a reliability of a life after death (I Cor 15:13-19). Jesus died to unite us with God by taking away our sins. Christianity has no stand if resurrection did not happen, we would have suffered in vain and placed our faith in false hope
LESSON OUTLINES
THE SIGNIFICANCE OF JESUSâ RESURRECTION:
Jesusâ resurrection is the Fatherâs signal that Jesus is His son and that he conquered death and he reign as Lord forever. As no one has ever died and woke from death. Rom 1:4, Rom 4: 25
Resurrection of Jesus Christ makes us to believe all His promises. If He did not rise after promising several times, none of His promises can be trusted. Matt 12:40, 16:21, 17:9 & 23, 20:19, 26:32.
Resurrection of Jesus Christ is the foundation of our apostolic faith. It is the bedrock of the new covenant. (Matt 16:18, Matt 26:31-32, I Cor 15:17)
Without resurrection of Jesus Christ, there will be no model for sacrificial living. Jesus lived a selfless life until his death. His resurrection was because of us, so He is an example to follow. (Matt 10:38-39, Acts 10:38-40)
Without resurrection, there will be no reckoning for sin (Acts 17:31)
THE HOPE WE HAVE
The most significant part of Easter is the hope of life after this world (Eternal life). He overcame death, he has power over it. So all the dead in Christ will be raised at the end and be with Him forever. The purpose of our dedication, commitment and perseverance is to reign with him at the end. His death and resurrection has given us the assurance that even though we die (physically), we shall live again (I Cor 15:19-20, I Thess 4:13-18)
LIFE APPLICATION
There is eternal life which has been secured through the death and resurrection of Christ, but you can only have the eternal life by reconciling with your maker. Let the purpose of His resurrection be fulfilled in your life.
