title: EXTRA OIL
memory_verse: Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
introduction: The utmost reward of the Christian faith and journey is to enter the kingdom of God. Jesus gave the parable of the ten virgins to admonish to prepare for the coming of Christ which comes before the millennial reign. The ten virgins represent the Christians. They were all invited to the wedding and were expecting the Groom, but lack of extra oil differentiates the virgins into two groups.
lesson_aim: To let you know that there are works to be done in order to enter the kingdom of God
application: There would not be room for restitution and reconciliation at rapture, live your life like rapture would happen in the next minute.
raw_text:
TOPIC: EXTRA OIL
AIM: To let you know that there are works to be done in order to enter the kingdom of God
MEMORY VERSE: Philippians 2:12; Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
BIBLE PASSAGE: Matthew 25:1-13
INTRODUCTION
The utmost reward of the Christian faith and journey is to enter the kingdom of God. Jesus gave the parable of the ten virgins to admonish to prepare for the coming of Christ which comes before the millennial reign. The ten virgins represent the Christians. They were all invited to the wedding and were expecting the Groom, but lack of extra oil differentiates the virgins into two groups.
LESSON OUTLINES
AN EXTRA OIL
The extra oil shows the level of preparedness of the two groups of virgins. They all believe that they bride is coming and were waiting for him as all Christians are waiting for the coming of Christ. The unwise virgins depict those Christians that are not prepared for the coming of Christ. The extra oil means that the five wise virgins have done extra work after receiving their salvation. The extra oil means;
They sanctified themselves â Rev 22:14
They made necessary restitution â Heb 12:14
They avoided worldliness â I John 2:15
They were forgiving â
They made sacrifices â Phil 4:12-13
They fought the good fight â II Tim 4:7
They kept the faith â II Tim 4:7
They endured persecution â II Cor 7:5
They worked on their adamic nature â I Cor 15:50
They walk and work as the spirit leads, there is no condemnation for them â Rom 8:1
THE FOOLISH VIRGINS
When the Groom came they started looking for extra oil. Which mean that they started trying to settle the unsettled matters, they wanted to be sanctified, they wanted to get rid of worldliness, but it was late. The rapture would be sudden that there would not be time to settle malice, disputes and other worldly things. There is still time to settle all the matters that now, the groom might arrive in the next minute.
LIFE APPLICATION
There would not be room for restitution and reconciliation at rapture, live your life like rapture would happen in the next minute.

title: TITHE
memory_verse: And blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him tithes of all.
introduction: Tithe is the one-tenth of all income you have gotten. God commanded us set it aside (Deut 14:22). The income could be salary, business profit, gift and others.  Tithe is different from voluntary giving/offering. It is specific (10%), unlike offering and other voluntary donation that has no specific amount.
lesson_aim: Tithing is Godâs command
application: Never see tithing as a burden, see it as a way of multiplying the remaining.
raw_text:
TOPIC: TITHE
AIM: Tithing is Godâs command
MEMORY VERSE: Genesis 14:20; And blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him tithes of all.
BIBLE PASSAGE: Malachi 3:7-12
INTRODUCTION
Tithe is the one-tenth of all income you have gotten. God commanded us set it aside (Deut 14:22). The income could be salary, business profit, gift and others.  Tithe is different from voluntary giving/offering. It is specific (10%), unlike offering and other voluntary donation that has no specific amount.
LESSON OUTLINES
TITHING
Tithing is a way of giving back to God and trusting Him for more blessings. It shows that we believe He is the provider of what we have and He can multiply the remaining we have. Accurate tithe is what God requested from us, if it is not up to ten percent it cannot be referred as Tithe. Tithe should be paid in/to the church of God where you are being fed with the word of God.
PURPOSE OF TITHING:
The tithe is for the expansion of the church work and ministry:
Paying pastors, ministers and other staff â Num 18:25-32
Maintenance of the church building
Purchase and repair of equipments
Funding church programmes, revival, evangelism and other outreaches
Supporting the poor and the needy in the church
Carrying out social responsibilities
BENEFITS OF TITHING
It helps us keep God first in our lives â Matt 6:21
It opens Godâs windows of blessings
It makes God to rebuke devourer
People will recognise you as blessed
Tithing is a way to avoid curses â Mal 3:9
It is a way of spreading the Gospel with our money
LIFE APPLICATION
Never see tithing as a burden, see it as a way of multiplying the remaining.

title: IRINAJO TITI LAILAI
memory_verse: Nitori tani ninu nyin ti npete ati ko ile-iso, ti ki yio ko joko ki o siro iye owo re, bi on ni to ti yio fi pari re.
introduction: Nigba ti a ba nmura sile fun igbeyawo, imura sile opolopo eniyan ma da lori ayeye igbeyawo. title: CHRISTIAN COURTSHIP
memory_verse: Can two walk together, except they be agreed?
introduction:
Courting is the period that precedes wedding. It is the time to identify differences and work out how to harmonize things. It is a time to set vision, hope and aspiration. It is the time to consolidate.  It is important to note that dating is different from courtship. Courtship is a relationship of people who have gotten Godâs leading about their partner, but dating is a trial approach to choosing lifeâs partner. In dating, if it does not work, you move to the next person. In Courtship, you are planning the way to make life easier and enjoy the wedding and marriage.
LESSON OULINES
IMPORTANCE OF COURTSHIP
This is the period to know each person intimately. Apart from knowing each other facially, where he/she works and his/her parent, it is the period to probe further to know his/her likes and dislike, strength and weakness. The type of family he/she wants to set up. It is the time to get parent consent (Judges 14:1-3). It is also time for marriage counsels. It is not the time to secretly indulge in sexual immoralities
QUESTIONS TO ASK DURING COURTSHIP
Are you born again?
What is your background? Biological, educational and others
What does marriage commitment mean to you?
What are your life goals?
What family size are we keeping?
Do you have children from your previous relationship?
What is your financial plan?
Are we keeping separate or joint account?
How are we handling bills?
How do you intend to resolve misunderstanding?
What does your spiritual life mean to you and your marriage?
Do we intend to attend same church?
How will you support your partner in chaotic work season?
How do you intend to set boundaries from external interference?
lesson_aim: To learn the importance of courtship and how to relate during courtship
application: Courtship is not an access to immoralities. It is a time to solidify the relationship by asking serious questions so that you can both prepare for the journey ahead.

title: ETO FIFE ARA-ENI SONA KRISTENI
memory_verse: Eni meji le rin po, bikosepe nwon re?
introduction: Fife ara eni sona je akoko ti o saju isopo. O je akoko lati mo iyato ti eni kini si enikeji, ki a si wa ona lati mu ki ibasepo wa. O je akoko lati ni afojusun, ireti ati ilepa ojo ola. O je akoko lati mu ohun gbogbo je okan. O se pataki lati jeki a mo pe, fife ara eni ninu aye ti won npe ni âdatingâ yato si ife ara eni sona. Fife ara eni sona je ibasepo larin awon meji ti won ti gba idari Olorun nipa eniti yio je enikeji won, sugbon dating je sise eyi je eyi o je lona ati ni alabarin. Ninu fife ara eni ninu aye (dating) ti nkan o ba lo bi awon mejeeji ti gbero, won ja ara ju sile, won o si tun lo sodo elomiran. Ninu Fife ara eni sona, a nse eto bi igbeaye yio se ro wa lorun, ti a si gbadun isopo ati igbeyawo wa.
lesson_aim: Lati ko pataki fife ara eni sona ati awon ibere ti o ye ka bere ni asiko na
application: Fife ara eni sona si se anfani lati se isekuse. O je asiko lati di okan ninu ajose yin nipa bibere awon ibere pataki ti yio mura yin sile fun irinajo ti o wa niwaju yin

Se o ti di atunbi?
Ibere nipa idile ti o ti wa ati iwe ti o ka. Ati awon ibere miran
Kini ifara-eni-ji/tabi nini ojuse ninu idile tumo si fun o?
Kini awon ilepa ati afojun re?
Omo melo ni a fe bi?
Se o ni omo kankan lati odo awon ti o ti fe sehin?
Kini ero ati eto re nipa isuna?
Se apo ifowo pamo kan ni a fe jo ni ni tabi otooto?

Se ile ijosin kan na ni o jo ma lo?

Bawo ni a o se fi gbedeke sile ki awon ara ita ma ba ri arin wa?

title: FAMILY BONDING
memory_verse: Behold, how good and pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
introduction: Family financial responsibility has made it difficult for members of the family to have time for leisure. Some people work in two or three places just to make ends meet. introduction: Relationship survival usually requires communication, intimacy and empathy. This does not exclude Christian relationships. We are human beings with blood flowing in our veins. Irrespective of the stage of the relationship (number of years in marriage), everyone wants to be loved and have tangible reason for staying in a relationship.
lesson_aim: Relationship should be nurtured, irrespective of the stage
application: Relationship is like a seed/plant, water it and give it the necessary nutrients

Irrespective of the stage of the relationship (number of years in marriage), everyone wants to be loved and have tangible reason for staying in a relationship.
LESSON OUTLINES
CAUSES OF PROBLEMS IN HOMES:
Inadequate preparation for marriage
Incompatibility of lifestyle
Dishonest behaviour
Infertility
Lack of commitment
Constant argument about believes
Parent intrusion/interference
WAYS TO AVOID PROBLEM IN OUR HOMES
Each partner should surrender to the leading of the Holy Spirit, this will make your home an enviable one.
Each partner should show love and empathy to the other as Jesus Christ showed love to the church.
Christianity does not mean that we should not spice up our relationship, do things that will make your relationship to grow and strong.
We should respect our partners and be committed to the relationship
Lack of money or child should be taken to God in prayer.
Avoid ungodly or unpleasant interference from anyone (including parents)
LIFE APPLICATION
Relationship is like a seed/plant, water it and give it the necessary nutrients

introduction: Spiritual weariness is a state of fatigue. You are feeling tired of continuing the journey. The zeal and passion with which you started the journey is not intact. Your faith has reduced and church is seen as routine or just an association.

INTRODUCTION

LESSON OUTLINES
CAUSES OF WEARINESS
Disappointments/battles e.g unanswered prayer
Giant obstacles â I kings 19:9-14
Persecution and opposition â Nehemiah 4:1-3
Recurrent demand for daily needs of life
Lack of gratitude from those you are serving
SIGNS OF WEARINESS
Lack of prayer
Irregular attendance of church programmes
Always complaining
Bitterness and being grumpy
Lack of zeal for kingdom work
Worldliness
Rebellion
HOW TO REGAIN STRENGTH
Focus on the reward from God â I Cor 15:58, Heb 6:10, Heb 12:2
Know the purpose/vision of your calling, do not let the challenges make you to lose focus

Trust Godâs timing â Hab 2:2-3, Job 14:14
Surround yourself with brethrens â Prov 27:17

In the Christian race you will be tired, but you must not stayed in that position for long, you must know how to regain strength.

title: ISIPOPADA

BIBELI KIKA: II Korinti 5:1-10
ORO AKOSO
Iku nsele ni ojoojumo ni ayika wa. Ki i se nkan ti o je ajooji si wa. Owe kan so wipe, iku ti o npa ojugba eni, owe ni o npa fun ni. Ti o tumo si wipe, o bowa kan eni na ni ojo kan. O seni lanu wipe, awon kan ko lati ka awon ikilo ti iku nse yi si, awon gba wipe iku je opin ohun gbogbo, awon kan si mura kale de tori won mo pe dandan ni iku.
PINPIN EKO
AWON OTITO NIPA IKU:
O je ibere isinmi ayeraye tabi ebi ayeraye. Ki i se opin ohun gbogbo (Matt 25:45)
Ko si eni ti o ni agbara ni ojo iku â Oniwasu 7:28, Oniwasu 8:8
O je nkan ti a o le sa fun â Heb 9:27, Oniwasu 12:7, Orin Dafidi 90:9-10
O ma nfi opolopo asiri han
O je sisi eniyan ni ipo kuro ni aye losi ayeraye â I Kor 15:40
BI IKU SE JE SI KRISTENI: Si awon oloto Kristeni, iku je ere (Fil 1:21)
O gbawa lowo irora inu aye ati eyi ti nbo â Rom 8:22-23, II Kor 5:2, Luku 16:24-25
A o fun okan wa ni itura ati ireti kuro lowo inunibibi inu aye â Ifihan 6:9-11, I Tess 1:7-9
A o ni iriri wipe a ti de ile, aye ki i se ile wa.
A o so emi wa di pipe â Heb 12:22-23
A o wa pelu Kristi â Fil 1:21-23

Iku ayeraye je opin ati iyapa titi lai kuro lodo Olorun. O je iya ayeraye ati yiya kuro lodo Olorun. Ko si atunse tabi ibalaje pelu Olorun mo ni ikorita yi. O je ipo idalebi ati ijiya ayeraye fun kiko Jesu gegebi ona ati gbigbe aye ti o lodi si ife Olorun.

introduction: Death happens every day around us. It is not something strange. There is an adage that says death that kills oneâs acquaintances is sending warning. Which implies that, it would be the personâs turn. Death is inevitable, so we should prepare for it.  It is unfortunate that some people decide to ignore the warning, some believe it is the end of everything and some decide to face the reality by preparing for the inevitable.
lesson_aim: Death is the beginning of an everlasting journey. It not the end, but a transition.

raw_text:
TOPIC: THE TRANSITION
AIM: Death is the beginning of an everlasting journey. It not the end, but a transition.
MEMORY VERSE: II Samuel 14:14; For we must needs die, and are as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God respect any person: yet doth he devise means, that his banished be not expelled from him.
BIBLE PASSAGE: II Corinthians 5:1-10
INTRODUCTION
Death happens every day around us. It is not something strange. There is an adage that says death that kills oneâs acquaintances is sending warning. Which implies that, it would be the personâs turn. Death is inevitable, so we should prepare for it.  It is unfortunate that some people decide to ignore the warning, some believe it is the end of everything and some decide to face the reality by preparing for the inevitable.
LESSON OUTLINES
FACTS ABOUT DEATH:
It is the beginning of rest or eternal damnation. It is not the end (Matt 25:45)
No one has power on the day of death â Eccl 7:28, Eccl 8:8
It is unavoidable â Heb 9:27, Eccl 12:7, Psalms 90:9-10
It exposes many secrets
It is the transition to eternity â I Cor 15:40
DEATH TO CHRISTIANS: To faithful Christians, Death is a gain (Phil 1:21)
We will be relieved of pain of the world and thereafter â Rom 8:22-23, II Cor 5:2, Luke 16:24-25
We will be given rest in our soul from the persecutions of the earth â Rev 6:9-11, I Thess 1:7-9
We will experience homeness, the earth is not our home.
Our spirit will be made perfect â Hebrew 12:22-23
We will be with Christ â Phil 1:21-23
ETERNAL DEATH â Psalm 9:17, Psalm 37:9, Daniel 12:2
Eternal death is final and permanent separation from God. It is a continuous suffering and exclusion from God. There is no remedy and reconciliation at this stage. It is the stage of eternal condemnation and punishment for rejecting Jesus as the way and living contrary to the will of God.
LIFE APPLICATION
For Christians, death is not to be feared but should be seen as a gateway to relieve and reward.

memory_verse: Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.
introduction: Finishing well is something we all desire. No one wants to fall flat in the journey or end in shame after serving God. But if we read through the history of Godâs children, we see numerous people who started well but did not end so well. There is need to plan how to end well, especially now that the end is near. We are at end of the world and events are indicating that the end is near. Most of the prophecies of Jesus Christ on the events that will precede the coming of the Lord are happening already.
lesson_aim: To know the forces we are fighting against and how to plan to end the race well
application: To finish well, we must overcome all the obstacles. Pray for the grace to overcome them.
raw_text:
TOPIC: FINISHING WELL
AIM: To know the forces we are fighting against and how to plan to end the race well
MEMORY VERSE: Colossians 3:2; Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.
BIBLE PASSAGE: II Timothy 4:7-8
INTRODUCTION
Finishing well is something we all desire. No one wants to fall flat in the journey or end in shame after serving God. But if we read through the history of Godâs children, we see numerous people who started well but did not end so well. There is need to plan how to end well, especially now that the end is near. We are at end of the world and events are indicating that the end is near. Most of the prophecies of Jesus Christ on the events that will precede the coming of the Lord are happening already.
LESSON OUTLINES
OBSTACLES ON THE WAY:
We are fighting against flesh, world and Satan.
Flesh: The corrupt desire within us which we have been obeying in ignorance but the knowledge of Godâs commandments has made us realise that it is a sin. The flesh is trying to hold us captive again. Romans 7:4-25, 8:5-14
World: The world and the church are two distinct groups. The world is under the control of the Satan, while the true church is under the control of God. The world consists of all evil, immoral, sinful pleasure, lukewarmness and indifference to God. Devil use the system of the world to persecute the believers. John 16:2-3, Matt 5:10-12, Rom 8:22-23
Satan: Christian faces spiritual battle with Satan and evil spirits (Matt 4:10). These power of darkness are the spiritual rulers of this world (II Cor 4:4, John 12:31). They energizes ungodliness (Eph 2:2), opposes Godâs will (Matt 13:38-39) and frequently attack the believers in the world (I Pet 5:8).
PLANS FOR FINISHING WELL
These are some of the ways we can plan to finish our race very well;
Daily commitment as a living sacrifice (Romans 12:1-2)
Stay connected to God through regular intake of His word and prayer (I Thess 5:17)
Regular review of yourself â what are the things you denounce? Are you not going back to them? What was your level of dedication to God, and how is it now? Is your prayer and bible study time intact? II Cor 13:5
Mortify the deeds of the flesh (Romans 8:13)
Manage your anxiety appropriately
Do not give room for pride, stay teachable. (Rom 12:3)
Accept the way God is dealing with you, it is a sign that you are His child and you are growing (Heb 12)
Keep an eternal perspective (Matt 25:21, Col 3:2)
Be principled and disciplined (I Cor 9:23-24)
Most of all, pray regularly for the grace of God to sustain you throughout the journey. (Eph 2:9, Heb 4:16, Heb 12:28)
LIFE APPLICATION
To finish well, we must overcome all the obstacles. Pray for the grace to overcome them.

title: PIPARI DARADARA
memory_verse: E ma ronu awon nkan ti mbe loke ki ise awon nkan ti mbe li aiye.
introduction: Pipari daradara je nkan ti gbogbo eniyan nfe. Ko si eni ti o fe subu ninu irin ajo tabi pari pelu itiju leyin ti o ti sin Olorun. Sugbon ti a ba wo itan awon omo Olorun, a o ri opolopo eniyan ti won bere daradara, ti won o si pari daradara. O ye ki a ni eto bi a o se pari daradara, papa julo ni asiko yi ti opin ti sunmo. A ti wa ni opin aye awon isele ti o nsele nfi han pe opin ti sunmo. Awon asotele Jesu Kristi nipa awon isele ti yio sele saju wiwa Oun ni o ti nsele bayi
lesson_aim: Lati mo awon ota ti a nba jagun ati bi a sele mura sile lati pari daradara
application: Lati pari daradara, a gbodo bori gbogbo idiwo. Gbadura fun oreofe lati bori won.
raw_text:
AKORI EKO: PIPARI DARADARA
ERONGBA: Lati mo awon ota ti a nba jagun ati bi a sele mura sile lati pari daradara
AKOSORI: Kolosse 3:2; E ma ronu awon nkan ti mbe loke ki ise awon nkan ti mbe li aiye.
BIBELI KIKA: II Timoteu 4:7-8
ORO AKOSO
Pipari daradara je nkan ti gbogbo eniyan nfe. Ko si eni ti o fe subu ninu irin ajo tabi pari pelu itiju leyin ti o ti sin Olorun. Sugbon ti a ba wo itan awon omo Olorun, a o ri opolopo eniyan ti won bere daradara, ti won o si pari daradara. O ye ki a ni eto bi a o se pari daradara, papa julo ni asiko yi ti opin ti sunmo. A ti wa ni opin aye awon isele ti o nsele nfi han pe opin ti sunmo. Awon asotele Jesu Kristi nipa awon isele ti yio sele saju wiwa Oun ni o ti nsele bayi
PINPIN EKO
AWON IDIWO NI OJU ONA:
A nba ara, aye ati esu ja.
Ara: O je ero idibaje ninu wa ti a ti ntele ni aimo sugbon oye ase Olorun jeki a mo pee se ni. Ara fe ko wa ni igbekun pada - Romu 7:4-25, 8:5-14.
Aye: Aye ati ijo yato si ara won. Aye wa labe idari esu, nigbati ijo Olorun tooto wa labe idari Olorun. Aye kun fun ibi, iwa ti o dara, ifekufe ese, kogbona-kotutu ati iwa aibikita si Olorun. Esu nlo igbekale ti aye lati fi se inunibini si awon onigbagbo. Johanu 16:2-3, Matt 5:10-12, Rom 8:22-23
Esu: Kristeni nkoju ija pelu esu ati emi buburu (Matt 4:10). Awon agbara okunkun yi je oludari aye lati inu emi okunkun (II Kor 4:4, Johanu 12:31). Won je aiwabi-Olorun ki tan kale (Efe 2:2), won tako ife Olorun (Matt 13:38-39), won si ma dojuko awon onigbagbo ni igba de igba (I Pet 5:8).
AWON ONA LATI PARI DARADARA
Awon ona ti a le fi mura sile lati pari ere ije wa daradara ni yi;
Ifara-eni-ji lojoojumo gegebi ebo aye mimo (Romu 12:1-2)
Sisunmo Olorun nipa kika oro Olorun ati adura gbigba deede (I Tess 5:17)
Ayewo ara eni ni igba de igba â Kini awon nkan ti o ti ko sile? Se o ti ma pada sinu awon nkan na? Bawo ni ifara-eni-ji re se ri si Olorun tele, bawo ni o se ri nisinyi? Se wakati adura ati asaro oro Olorun re si se deede? II Kor 13:5
Pipa eya ara wa ti o wa ni aye run (Romu 8:13)
Se akoso awon ireti ati afojunsun re bi o ti ye
Mase fi aye gba igberaga, je eniti o se ko. (Romu 12:3)
Fi ara bale gba bi Olorun se nko o tabi to o, o je ami wipe o je omo Olorun ati wipe o ndagba (Heb 12)
Ni afojusun orun/ayeraye (Matt 25:21, Kol 3:2)
Je eniti o gba ibawi, ti o si duro lori ese re (I Kor 9:23-24)
Lakotan, ma gbadura fun oreofe Olorun ni igba gbogbo ki o le ran o lowo ninu irinajo na. (Efe 2:9, Heb 4:16, Heb 12:28)
LILO EKO NA
Lati pari daradara, a gbodo bori gbogbo idiwo. Gbadura fun oreofe lati bori won.

title: APERE RERE
memory_verse: Mase jeki enikeni ki o gan ewe re; sugbon ki iwo ki o je apre fun awon ti o gbagbo, ninu oro, ninu iwa hihu, ninu ife, ninu emi, ninu igbagbo, ninu iwa mimo.
introduction: Iwai pa ati ibi po si ni awujo wa. Ko si eniti o ro tomo enikeji ki won to gbe igbese. Ole jija, ireje, arekereke, etan ni awon eniyan nse lati fi ri owo ti won si npa elomiran lara. A je asoju Kristi, a si gbodo yato si awon elomiran. Isoro wa gbodo fi Kristi han (Fil 1:27, I Pet 1:15), iwa wa gbodo je eyi ti awon eniyan yio fe fi se awokose (I Kor 11:1), imotara eni nikan ko gbodo farahan ninu awon igbese wa (Marku 6:17-28). A je digi Olorun fun isoore, anu ati ife ninu aye. Jesu fi ife han si aye, a gbodo se afihan awon iwa wonyi si awon ara aye.
lesson_aim: Lati jeki o mo wipe, o ye ki o je apere rere gegebi asoju Olorun ni aye.
application: Jesu o si ni aye, sugbon a je asoju re lati jeki aye ni iriri awon oun ti Jesu se nigbati o wa ni aye. Se wa je asoju rere fun Kristi?
raw_text:
AKORI EKO: APERE RERE
ERONGBA: Lati jeki o mo wipe, o ye ki o je apere rere gegebi asoju Olorun ni aye.
AKOSORI: I Timoteu 4:12; Mase jeki enikeni ki o gan ewe re; sugbon ki iwo ki o je apre fun awon ti o gbagbo, ninu oro, ninu iwa hihu, ninu ife, ninu emi, ninu igbagbo, ninu iwa mimo.
BIBELI KIKA: Efesu 4:17-32
ORO AKOSO
Iwai pa ati ibi po si ni awujo wa. Ko si eniti o ro tomo enikeji ki won to gbe igbese. Ole jija, ireje, arekereke, etan ni awon eniyan nse lati fi ri owo ti won si npa elomiran lara. A je asoju Kristi, a si gbodo yato si awon elomiran. Isoro wa gbodo fi Kristi han (Fil 1:27, I Pet 1:15), iwa wa gbodo je eyi ti awon eniyan yio fe fi se awokose (I Kor 11:1), imotara eni nikan ko gbodo farahan ninu awon igbese wa (Marku 6:17-28). A je digi Olorun fun isoore, anu ati ife ninu aye. Jesu fi ife han si aye, a gbodo se afihan awon iwa wonyi si awon ara aye.
PINPIN EKO
AWON TI A LE FI APERE HAN:
Awon alaigbagbo o gba enikeni gbo mo, boya o je Kristeni abi o ki i se Kristeni, nitori lara won ni a tan je, ja ni ole, ti a si ti reje lodo awon kan ti won pe ara won ni Kristeni. A ko gbodo fenu je Kristeni lasan, sugbon ki a fi han nipa fifi fun awon eniyan, idariji, fifi ife han, jije olooto, gbigba awon eniyan ni imoran, adura gbigba, awon iranlowo ti o se foju ri.
JIJE ASOJU RERE KI I SE IWA ALAIGBON:
Nigbati o ba wuwa daradara, awon eniyan yio momo pa o lara, won o fie to re dun o, lati ri boya o ma gbesan. Mase gbesan tabi ka si won lorun. Awon ore re yio pe o ni alaigbon tabi ode nitori o ko lati gbesan. O ki nse ode. Suuru je okan lara awon isura onigbagbo tooto. Jeki Olorun o gbe o nija lori oro na (Rom 12:19, II Tess 1:5-8)
LILO EKO NA
Jesu o si ni aye, sugbon a je asoju re lati jeki aye ni iriri awon oun ti Jesu se nigbati o wa ni aye. Se wa je asoju rere fun Kristi?

title: GOOD EXAMPLE
memory_verse: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
introduction: Wickedness and evil abound in our society. No one consider the feeling of others before acting. Stealing, cheating, manipulation, blackmail are what people do to make money at the detriment of others. We are ambassadors of Christ and should be different from others. Our conversation should show Christ (Phil 1:27, I Pet 1:15), our behaviour should be what people would want to emulate (I Cor 11:1), our motive and purpose of doing things should not depict selfishness (Mark 6:17-28). We are the mirror of Godâs goodness, kindness and love to the world. Jesus shows love to the world, we should show samples of that to the people in the world.
lesson_aim: To let you know that you are to be a good example as Godâs representative on earth.
application: Jesus is not in the world but we are His representative to let the world experience what Jesus did while on earth. Will you be a good ambassador of Christ?
raw_text:
TOPIC: GOOD EXAMPLE
AIM: To let you know that you are to be a good example as Godâs representative on earth.
MEMORY VERSE: I Timothy 4:12; Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
BIBLE PASSAGE: Ephesians 4:17-32
INTRODUCTION
Wickedness and evil abound in our society. No one consider the feeling of others before acting. Stealing, cheating, manipulation, blackmail are what people do to make money at the detriment of others. We are ambassadors of Christ and should be different from others. Our conversation should show Christ (Phil 1:27, I Pet 1:15), our behaviour should be what people would want to emulate (I Cor 11:1), our motive and purpose of doing things should not depict selfishness (Mark 6:17-28). We are the mirror of Godâs goodness, kindness and love to the world. Jesus shows love to the world, we should show samples of that to the people in the world.
LESSON OUTLINES
PRACTICAL WAYS TO SHOW EXAMPLE:
Unbelievers do not believe anybody again, either you call yourself a Christian or not, because some of them have been duped, deceived and cheated by some people who called themselves Christians. We should not just profess to be a Christian but show that in practical ways like gifting, forgiveness, loving, honesty, counselling, prayer, physical assistance etc.
BEING A GOOD EXAMPLE IS NO FOOLISHNES:
When you are being good, people would intentional hurt you and deprive you of your right expecting you to retaliate. Do not revenge or take offense. Some of your friends would call you a fool or abandon you because you decided not to revenge. You are not a fool. Patience is one of the virtues of a true believer. Let God avenge the matter (Rom 12:19, II Thess 1:5-8)
LIFE APPLICATION
Jesus is not in the world but we are His representative to let the world experience what Jesus did while on earth. Will you be a good ambassador of Christ?
